title.zh: 卷一百二十一 列傳第七十一: 僕固懷恩 梁崇義 李懷光
title.en: Volume 121 Biographies 71: Pugu Huai'en, Liang Chongyi, Li Huaiguan
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 列傳第七十一: 僕固懷恩 梁崇義 李懷光 Volume 121 Biographies 71: Pugu Huai'en, Liang Chongyi, Li Huaiguan

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩梁崇義李懷光

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en, Liang Chongyi, Li Huaiguang
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en, Liang Chongyi, and Li Huaiguang

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩，鐵勒部落仆骨歌濫拔延之曾孫，語訛謂之仆固。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en was the great-grandson of Geli Ge Ganbozhen of the Tiele tribe Pugu; through a corruption of the name they were called Pugu.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was the great-grandson of Geli Ge Ganbozhen of the Tiele Pugu clan; a corruption of the name had led the family to be known as the Pugu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，鐵勒九姓大首領率其部落來降，分置瀚海、燕然、金微、幽陵等九都督府於夏州，別為蕃州以禦邊，授歌濫拔延為右武衛大將軍、金微都督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, the great chiefs of the nine Tiele surnames led their tribes to submit. Nine protectorates—Hanhai, Yanran, Jinwei, Youling, and the rest—were established at Xia Prefecture, and Fanzhou was set apart to guard the frontier. Ganbozhen was appointed Right Martial Guard general and Jinwei protector.
translations.idiomatic: In 646, the principal chiefs of the nine Tiele clans brought their people to surrender. Nine protectorates, including Hanhai, Yanran, Jinwei, and Youling, were placed under Xia Prefecture, while Fanzhou was established separately to defend the border. Ganbozhen was made Right Martial Guard general and protector of Jinwei.

sentences.zh: 拔延生乙李啜拔，乙李啜拔生懷恩，世襲都督。

translations.literal: Ganbozhen begot Yili Chueba; Yili Chueba begot Huai'en. The post of protector was inherited in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Ganbozhen's son was Yili Chueba, and Yili Chueba's son was Huai'en. The family held the protectorate in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，加左領軍大將軍同正員、特進。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he was additionally appointed Left Army general of the same rank and special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao period he was further promoted to Left Army general with concurrent status and granted the title of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 歷事節度王忠嗣、安思順，皆以善格鬥，達諸蕃情，有統御材，委之心腹。

translations.literal: He successively served under the military governors Wang Zhongsi and An Sishun. In each case, because he excelled at hand-to-hand combat, understood the sentiments of the various frontier peoples, and possessed talent for command, they entrusted him as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn under the governors Wang Zhongsi and An Sishun. Both men valued his prowess in combat, his grasp of frontier affairs, and his gift for leadership, and each treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，從郭子儀討高秀巖於雲中，破之，又敗薛忠義於背度山下，抗賊七千騎，生擒忠義男，襲下馬邑郡。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he followed Guo Ziyi to attack Gao Xiuyan at Yunzhong and defeated him. He again defeated Xue Zhongyi below Beidu Mountain, withstood seven thousand rebel horsemen, captured Zhongyi's son alive, and stormed Mayi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Huai'en followed Guo Ziyi against Gao Xiuyan at Yunzhong and routed him. He next defeated Xue Zhongyi at the foot of Beidu Mountain, held off seven thousand rebel cavalry, took Zhongyi's son prisoner, and seized Mayi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十五載，進軍與李光弼合勢，及史思明戰於常山、趙郡、沙河、嘉山，皆大破之，懷恩功居多。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he advanced with Li Guangbi in combined force and fought Shi Siming at Changshan, Zhao Commandery, Shahe, and Jiashan. In each engagement the rebels were thoroughly defeated, and Huai'en's achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In 756 he marched with Li Guangbi, and together they fought Shi Siming at Changshan, Zhao, Shahe, and Jiashan. Each battle ended in a decisive victory, with Huai'en contributing more than any other commander.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位於靈武，懷恩從郭子儀赴行在所。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne at Lingwu, Huai'en followed Guo Ziyi to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong was enthroned at Lingwu, Huai'en accompanied Guo Ziyi to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 時同羅部落自西京叛賊，北寇朔方，子儀與懷恩擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the Tongluo tribe had broken from the rebels at the Western Capital and was raiding north into Shuofang. Guo Ziyi and Huai'en attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo had deserted the rebels at Chang'an and were raiding north into Shuofang. Guo Ziyi and Huai'en moved against them.

sentences.zh: 懷恩子玢領徒擊賊，兵敗而降，尋又自拔而歸，懷恩叱而斬之。

translations.literal: Huai'en's son Bin led troops against the rebels, was defeated and surrendered, then shortly broke free and returned. Huai'en rebuked him and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's son Bin led a detachment against the enemy, was beaten and surrendered, then soon escaped and came back. Huai'en denounced him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 將士懾駭，無不一當百，遂破同羅千餘騎於河上，盡收其器械、駝馬。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were awed and shaken; each fought as if worth a hundred men. They thereupon broke more than a thousand Tongluo horsemen on the river and seized all their weapons, camels, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were stunned into ferocity, and every man fought as though he were worth a hundred. They routed more than a thousand Tongluo cavalry on the riverbank and captured all their arms, camels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 肅宗雖仗朔方之眾，將假蕃兵以張形勢，乃遣懷恩與燉煌王承寀使於回紇，請兵結好。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Suzong relied on the forces of Shuofang, he intended to borrow barbarian troops to magnify his posture and therefore sent Huai'en with Prince of Dunhuang Chengcai as envoys to the Uyghurs to request troops and form an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Though Suzong depended on the Shuofang army, he wished to augment his strength with allied nomad forces and sent Huai'en with Prince Chengcai of Dunhuang to the Uyghurs to seek troops and a treaty.

sentences.zh: 回紇可汗遂以女妻承寀，兼請公主，遣首領隨懷恩入朝。

translations.literal: The Uyghur khan thereupon gave his daughter in marriage to Chengcai and also requested an imperial princess, sending chieftains to follow Huai'en to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur khan married his daughter to Chengcai, asked for a Tang princess in return, and sent chieftains to accompany Huai'en to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，又從子儀下馮翊、河東二郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he again followed Guo Ziyi in reducing the two commanderies of Fengyi and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 757 he again followed Guo Ziyi in the capture of Fengyi and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 走偽將崔乾祐，又襲破潼關。

translations.literal: He routed the rebel general Cui Qianyou and again stormed and took Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He drove off the rebel general Cui Qianyou and then stormed and retook Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊將安守忠、李歸仁自京率眾來援，苦戰二日，官軍敗績。

translations.literal: The rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren led troops from the capital to relieve the siege. After two days of bitter fighting, the government army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren marched from the capital with reinforcements. After two days of fierce combat, the imperial forces were beaten.

sentences.zh: 懷恩退至渭水，無舟楫，抱馬以渡，存者僅半，乃奔歸子儀於河東，整其餘眾。

translations.literal: Huai'en withdrew to the Wei River. With no boats, he clasped his horse to swim across; barely half survived. He then fled back to Guo Ziyi in Hedong and reorganized the remaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en fell back to the Wei River. There were no boats, so he clung to his horse to swim across; only about half his men survived. He rejoined Guo Ziyi in Hedong and rallied what was left of the force.

sentences.zh: 四月，子儀赴鳳翔，李歸仁以勁卒五千邀之於三原北。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Guo Ziyi went to Fengxiang. Li Guiren intercepted him north of Sanyuan with five thousand crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guo Ziyi marched toward Fengxiang. Li Guiren blocked his path north of Sanyuan with five thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 子儀窘急，使懷恩及王升、陳回光、渾釋之、李國貞等五將伏兵於白渠留運橋以待之，賊至伏發，歸仁大敗而走。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was in dire straits and sent Huai'en with Wang Sheng, Chen Huiguang, Hun Shizhi, Li Guozhen, and four other generals to lay an ambush at the Liuyun Bridge on the Bai Canal. When the rebels arrived the ambush was sprung and Guiren was thoroughly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Guo Ziyi sent Huai'en and four other generals—Wang Sheng, Chen Huiguang, Hun Shizhi, and Li Guozhen—to lie in wait at Liuyun Bridge on the Bai Canal. When the rebels came up, the trap was sprung and Guiren was routed.

sentences.zh: 又從子儀戰於清渠，不利，歸於鳳翔。

translations.literal: He again followed Guo Ziyi in battle at Qingqu, with an unfavorable outcome, and returned to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again with Guo Ziyi at Qingqu, but the battle went badly, and they withdrew to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 及回紇使葉護、帝得數千騎來赴國難，南蠻、大食之卒相繼而至。

translations.literal: When the Uyghur envoy Yehu and the emperor obtained several thousand horsemen to come to the dynasty's aid, troops of the southern barbarians and of Dashi arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur forces under Yehu and several thousand cavalry sent by the emperor arrived to aid the dynasty, followed in turn by troops from the southern tribes and from the Abbasid realm.

sentences.zh: 肅宗乃遣廣平王為元帥，以子儀為副，而懷恩領回紇兵從之澧水。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong thereupon appointed the Prince of Guangping as commander-in-chief, with Guo Ziyi as deputy, while Huai'en led Uyghur troops in following him to the Li River.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong then named the Prince of Guangping supreme commander, with Guo Ziyi as his deputy, while Huai'en led the Uyghur contingent with them to the Li River.

sentences.zh: 賊伏兵於營東，懷恩引回紇馳殺之，匹馬不歸，賊乃大潰。

translations.literal: The rebels had hidden troops east of the camp. Huai'en led the Uyghurs in a charge to slaughter them; not a single horse returned, and the rebels thereupon collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops lay in ambush east of the camp. Huai'en led the Uyghurs in a headlong charge that wiped them out to the last horse, and the rebel army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 日暮，懷恩謂王曰：「賊必棄城走矣，請以二百騎馬追之，縛取李歸仁、田乾真、安守忠、張通儒。」

translations.literal: At dusk Huai'en said to the prince: "The rebels are certain to abandon the city and flee. I ask leave to pursue with two hundred horsemen and bind and capture Li Guiren, Tian Qianzhen, An Shouzhong, and Zhang Tongru."
translations.idiomatic: As evening fell, Huai'en told the prince, "The rebels are sure to abandon the city and run. Let me take two hundred horsemen in pursuit and bring back Li Guiren, Tian Qianzhen, An Shouzhong, and Zhang Tongru in bonds."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「將軍戰亦疲矣，且休息，迨明而後圖之。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "General, you too are weary from battle. Rest for now and plan again after daybreak."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, "You are exhausted from fighting as it is. Rest tonight and we will decide at dawn."

sentences.zh: 懷恩曰：「歸仁、守忠，天下驍賊也，聚勝而敗，此天與我也，奈何縱之不取？

translations.literal: Huai'en said: "Guiren and Shouzhong are the fiercest rebels under heaven. They have gathered victory only to be defeated—this is Heaven's gift to me. How can we let them go and not seize them?
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en said, "Guiren and Shouzhong are the fiercest rebels in the realm. They had victory in hand and still lost—Heaven has handed them to us. How can we let them slip away?

sentences.zh: 若使得眾，復為我患，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: If they are allowed to gather followers again, they will once more become a trouble to us, and even regret will be of no avail.
translations.idiomatic: If they rally their forces again, they will be our trouble once more, and regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 夫戰尚速，何明日為？」

translations.literal: In warfare what matters is speed—why wait until tomorrow?"
translations.idiomatic: In war, speed is everything—why put it off until tomorrow?"

sentences.zh: 王固止之，令還營。

translations.literal: The prince firmly restrained him and ordered him back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held firm and sent him back to camp.

sentences.zh: 懷恩又固請，往而復反，一夕四五起。

translations.literal: Huai'en again pressed his request insistently, going out and returning repeatedly, rising four or five times in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en pressed his case again and again, leaving camp and coming back repeatedly, getting up four or five times that night alone.

sentences.zh: 遲明諜至，守忠等果逃。

translations.literal: Near dawn scouts arrived reporting that Shouzhong and the others had indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: At first light scouts reported that Shouzhong and the others had indeed escaped.

sentences.zh: 又從王大破賊於陜西之新店，收兩京，皆立殊功。

translations.literal: He again followed the prince in thoroughly defeating the rebels at Xindian in Shaanxi, recovering the two capitals, and in each case establishing outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the prince to a crushing victory at Xindian in Shaanxi and took part in the recovery of both capitals, earning distinguished merit in each campaign.

sentences.zh: 以前後功加開府儀同三司、鴻臚卿同正員、同節度副使。

translations.literal: For his successive achievements he was additionally appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of an independent office, concurrent chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and concurrent deputy military governor.
translations.idiomatic: For these cumulative feats he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with an independent office, made concurrent chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and named concurrent deputy military governor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，封豐國公，食實封二百戶。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was enfeoffed as Duke of Feng with an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was created Duke of Feng with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年九月，遣九節度擊安慶緒於相州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianyuan, nine military governors were dispatched to attack An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Qianyuan 1, nine military governors were sent to attack An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀領朔方行營，破安太清，下懷、衛二州，圍相州，戰愁思崗。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Ziyi in leading the Shuofang field army, defeated An Taiqing, took Huaizhou and Weizhou, besieged Xiang Prefecture, and fought at Chousi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi at the head of the Shuofang field army, defeated An Taiqing, took Huaizhou and Weizhou, besieged Xiangzhou, and fought at Chousi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 凡經五月，常為先鋒，堅敵大陣，必經其戰，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Over five months he was constantly the vanguard; whenever the enemy formed a solid line, he had to fight through it, and his courage surpassed all three armies.
translations.idiomatic: For five months he was always in the vanguard. Whenever the enemy formed a solid battle line, he fought through it, and his courage outshone the whole army.

sentences.zh: 尋充都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made overall commander of army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made overall commander of army and horse.

sentences.zh: 及李光弼代子儀，懷恩又副之。

translations.literal: When Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi, Huai'en again served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi, Huai'en again served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，進封大寧郡王，遷御史大夫、朔方行營節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan he was advanced to Prince of Daning Commandery and transferred to Censor-in-Chief and commander of the Shuofang field army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 2 he was advanced to Prince of Daning and made Censor-in-Chief and commander of the Shuofang field army.

sentences.zh: 又從李光弼守河陽，破周出，擒徐璜玉、安太清，拔懷州，皆摧鋒陷敵，功冠諸將。

translations.literal: Again following Li Guangbi in defending Heyang, he defeated Zhou Chu, captured Xu Huangyu and An Taiqing, and retook Huaizhou—in each case breaking the enemy vanguard and penetrating their ranks, his achievements surpassing all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Again following Li Guangbi in the defense of Heyang, he defeated Zhou Chu, captured Xu Huangyu and An Taiqing, and retook Huaizhou. Each time he broke the enemy vanguard and drove deep into their ranks, and his achievements surpassed every other general.

sentences.zh: 其男瑒又以開府儀同三司從將兵於其軍，每深入虜陣，以勇敢聞，軍中號為「鬥將」。

translations.literal: His son Chang also served as Palace Attendant of the First Rank with the Same Privileges as the Three Dukes, leading troops in his army; each time he penetrated deep into the enemy formation and became known for valor, and the army called him the "battle general."
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang, serving as Palace Attendant of the First Rank with the Same Privileges as the Three Dukes, led troops in his army. Each time he drove deep into the enemy lines and won renown for courage, and the army called him the "battle general."

sentences.zh: 懷恩為人雄毅寡言，應對舒緩，而剛決犯上，始居偏裨之中，意有不合，雖主將必詬怒之。

translations.literal: Huai'en as a man was bold and resolute, sparing of speech, unhurried in reply, yet firm and decisive and prone to offend his superiors. When he first held a subordinate command, if anything did not accord with his mind he would revile and rage even at the commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was a man of fierce resolve who spoke little and answered slowly, yet he was stubborn and quick to defy authority. Even as a junior officer, if he disagreed with something he would lash out at his commander without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀為帥，以寬厚容眾，素重懷恩，其麾下皆朔方蕃漢勁卒，恃功怙將，多為不法，子儀每事優容之，行師用兵，倚以輯事。

translations.literal: When Guo Ziyi was commander, by his generous forbearance toward the masses he had long valued Huai'en. Those under his command were all crack Shuofang troops, both barbarian and Han, who relied on their achievements and trusted in their generals and often acted unlawfully. Guo Ziyi always treated them with indulgence on every matter and, in campaigning and employing troops, relied on them to bring affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi commanded with a broad tolerance that won men's loyalty, and he had long held Huai'en in high regard. His troops were the hard-fighting Shuofang veterans, both nomad and Han, who leaned on their battle honors and their generals and often bent the law. Guo Ziyi indulged them on every count and depended on them to hold his campaigns together.

sentences.zh: 而光弼持法嚴肅，法不貸下，懷恩心憚而頗不葉。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi, by contrast, upheld the law with stern severity and would not spare subordinates. Huai'en feared him inwardly and was rather ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi, by contrast, enforced the law with iron rigor and showed no leniency to subordinates. Huai'en feared him and was never quite at ease under his command.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，從李光弼與史思明戰於邙山，不利。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he followed Li Guangbi in fighting Shi Siming at Mount Mang, with an unfavorable outcome.
translations.idiomatic: In 761 he followed Li Guangbi against Shi Siming at Mount Mang, but the battle went badly.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以懷恩功高，恩顧特異諸將，至冬，加工部尚書，敕李輔國及常參官送上，太官造食以寵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong, because Huai'en's achievements were lofty, showed him favor and regard distinct from other generals. By winter he was additionally appointed Minister of Works. An edict ordered Li Fuguo and the regular attending officials to escort him in presentation, and the imperial kitchen prepared food to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huai'en's merits were so great, Suzong favored him above the other generals. That winter he was made Minister of Works, with orders for Li Fuguo and the regular court officials to escort him to audience and for the imperial kitchen to prepare a feast in his honor.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，拜隴右節度，未行，改朔方行營節度，以副郭子儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Huai'en was appointed military governor of Longyou. Before he departed, the appointment was changed to military governor of the Shuofang field headquarters, serving as deputy to Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong succeeded to the throne, Huai'en was appointed governor of Longyou, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned as governor of the Shuofang field command, serving under Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 其秋，上使中官劉清潭請兵於回紇登裏可汗，登裏已為史朝義誘之傾國入塞，眾號十萬，關中騷擾，上使殿中監樂子昂馳於塞上勞之，遇於忻州。

translations.literal: That autumn the emperor sent the eunuch Liu Qingtan to request troops from the Uyghur khan Dengli. Dengli had already been enticed by Shi Chaoyi to bring his whole nation across the border; his forces were said to number one hundred thousand, and Guanzhong was thrown into alarm. The emperor sent the palace director Yue Zi'ang posthaste to the frontier to console them; he met them at Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor sent the eunuch Liu Qingtan to request troops from the Uyghur khan Dengli. Dengli had already been lured by Shi Chaoyi into leading his entire nation across the border in force—said to be a hundred thousand strong—and Guanzhong was in uproar. The emperor dispatched the palace director Yue Zi'ang to the frontier to welcome them, and Yue met the army at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，肅宗以寧國公主下嫁於毗伽闕可汗，毗伽闕可汗又以少子請婚，肅宗以懷恩女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Suzong had given the Princess of Ning in marriage to the Uyghur khan Boli Yabghu. Boli Yabghu also requested a marriage for his younger son, and Suzong gave him Huai'en's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Suzong had married the Princess of Ning to the Uyghur khan Boli Yabghu. When the khan asked for a bride for his younger son as well, Suzong gave him Huai'en's daughter.

sentences.zh: 毗伽可汗死，少子代立，即登裏可汗。

translations.literal: When the khan Boli died, the younger son succeeded in his place—this was Khan Dengli.
translations.idiomatic: When Boli Yabghu died, his younger son succeeded him as Khan Dengli.

sentences.zh: 登裏立，以懷恩女為可敦。

translations.literal: When Dengli took the throne, he made Huai'en's daughter his khatun.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession, Dengli made Huai'en's daughter his chief consort.

sentences.zh: 至是，可汗請與懷恩及懷恩之母相見，詔從之。

translations.literal: At this time the khan requested to meet Huai'en and Huai'en's mother. An edict granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Now the khan asked to meet Huai'en and his mother, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 懷恩嫌疑不敢，上因賜鐵券，手詔以遣之，即令其母便發。

translations.literal: Huai'en was suspicious and did not dare go. The emperor thereupon bestowed an iron certificate and sent him off with a personal edict, and at once ordered his mother to depart immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was wary and hesitated to go. The emperor gave him an iron certificate of immunity and a personal edict sending him on his way, and ordered his mother to set out at once.

sentences.zh: 懷恩與回紇可汗相見於太原，可汗大悅，遂許助討朝義，於是進兵，歷太原、汾、晉，營於陜州以俟期。

translations.literal: Huai'en met the Uyghur khan at Taiyuan. The khan was greatly pleased and thereupon promised to aid in attacking Chaoyi. He then advanced his army, passing through Taiyuan, Fen, and Jin, and encamped at Shaan Prefecture to await the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en met the Uyghur khan at Taiyuan. The khan was delighted and pledged to help crush Chaoyi. The army then marched through Taiyuan, Fen, and Jin and encamped at Shaanzhou to await the coordinated advance.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔天下兵馬元帥雍王為中軍先鋒，以懷恩為副，加同中書門下平章事，領河東、朔方節度行營及鎮西、回紇兵馬赴陜州，並令諸道節度一時齊進。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict appointed the Prince of Yong, commander-in-chief of all armies and horses under heaven, as vanguard of the central army, with Huai'en as deputy and additionally as Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs. He was to lead the Hedong and Shuofang field headquarters and the armies of Zhenxi and the Uyghurs to Shaan Prefecture, and all circuit military governors were ordered to advance together at one time.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court named the Prince of Yong supreme commander and vanguard of the central force, with Huai'en as his deputy and associate chief minister. Huai'en was to lead the Hedong and Shuofang field armies plus the Zhenxi and Uyghur contingents to Shaanzhou, while every regional governor was ordered to advance in concert.

sentences.zh: 懷恩與回紇左殺為先鋒，觀軍容使魚朝恩、陜州節度郭英乂為後殿，自澠池入；

translations.literal: Huai'en and the Uyghur Left Kill formed the vanguard; the army inspector Yu Chao'en and Shaan military governor Guo Yingyi formed the rear guard, entering from Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and the Uyghur Left Kill led the vanguard; Yu Chao'en, army inspector, and Guo Yingyi, governor of Shaan, brought up the rear, advancing from Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 陳鄭節度李抱玉自河陽入；

translations.literal: Chen-Zheng military governor Li Baoyu entered from Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu, governor of Chen and Zheng, entered from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 河南副元帥、雍王留陜州。

translations.literal: The deputy commander-in-chief of Henan, the Prince of Yong, remained at Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, deputy commander for Henan, stayed behind at Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷恩等師至黃水，賊徒數萬，堅柵自固。

translations.literal: When Huai'en's army reached Huangshui, rebel forces numbered in the tens of thousands and had fortified palisades to hold their ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en's force reached Huangshui, tens of thousands of rebels had thrown up fortified stockades.

sentences.zh: 懷恩陣於西原上，廣張旗幟以當之，命驍騎及回紇之眾傍南山出於東北，兩軍舉旗內應，表裏擊之，一鼓而拔，賊死者數萬。

translations.literal: Huai'en drew up his battle line on the western plain and spread banners wide to confront them. He ordered crack horsemen and Uyghur troops to skirt the southern mountains and emerge in the northeast. Both forces raised their banners in mutual signal and struck from within and without. At one drumbeat the position was taken; rebel dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en formed up on the western plain with banners flying wide to hold the enemy in place, while crack cavalry and Uyghur troops swung around the southern hills to strike from the northeast. At the signal of raised banners the two wings hit the camp from inside and out at once. A single charge carried the position, and tens of thousands of rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 朝義領鐵騎十萬來救，陣於昭覺寺，賊皆殊死決戰，短兵既接，相殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led one hundred thousand iron cavalry to the relief and drew up his line at Zhaojue Temple. The rebels all fought to the death; once close combat was joined, the mutual slaughter was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi marched to the rescue with a hundred thousand armored horsemen and formed battle lines at Zhaojue Temple. The rebels fought with desperate fury, and once hand-to-hand combat began the slaughter on both sides was immense.

sentences.zh: 官軍驟擊之，賊陣而不動。

translations.literal: The government army struck them suddenly, but the rebel formation did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial force charged, but the rebel line held firm.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩令射生五百人下馬，弓弩亂發，多中賊而死，陣亦如初。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en ordered five hundred archers to dismount and loose bows and crossbows in disorder. Many rebels were struck and killed, yet the formation remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en ordered five hundred archers to dismount and unleash a volley of arrows. Many rebels fell, yet the line did not break.

sentences.zh: 鎮西節度使馬璘曰：「事急矣！」

translations.literal: Zhenxi military governor Ma Lin said: "The situation is urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin, governor of Zhenxi, cried, "This is desperate!"

sentences.zh: 遂援旗而進，單騎奔擊，奪賊兩牌，突入萬眾之中，左右披靡，大軍乘之而入，朝義大敗，斬首一萬六千級，生擒四千六百人，降者三萬二千人。

translations.literal: He thereupon seized his banner and advanced, charging alone, seizing two rebel standards and plunging into the midst of ten thousand men. To left and right the enemy gave way, and the main army pressed in on their momentum. Chaoyi was thoroughly defeated: heads taken numbered sixteen thousand, captives four thousand six hundred, and those who surrendered thirty-two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his banner and charged alone, snatching two enemy standards and plunging into the mass of ten thousand men. The rebels parted before him, and the main army poured through the gap. Chaoyi was routed: sixteen thousand heads were taken, four thousand six hundred men captured, and thirty-two thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 轉戰於石榴園、老君廟，賊黨又敗，人馬蹂踐，填於尚書谷，朝義輕騎而走。

translations.literal: Fighting shifted to Shiliu Garden and Laojun Temple; the rebel party was again defeated. Men and horses trampled one another until they filled Shangshu Valley, and Chaoyi fled on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting moved to Shiliu Garden and Laojun Temple, where the rebels were beaten again. Men and horses piled up in Shangshu Valley, and Chaoyi fled with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 懷恩乃進收東京及河陽城，封其府庫，偽中書令許叔冀、王伷等，承制釋之，悉皆安堵。

translations.literal: Huai'en then advanced to recover the Eastern Capital and Heyang city, sealed their treasuries, and by imperial order released the rebel chief ministers Xu Shuji, Wang Ni, and others; all were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en then marched in to take the Eastern Capital and Heyang, sealed the treasuries, and by imperial order released the rebel ministers Xu Shuji, Wang Ni, and the rest. The populace was left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 懷恩留回紇可汗營於河陽，乃使其子右廂兵馬使瑒、北庭朔方兵馬使高輔成以步軍萬餘眾乘勝逐北。

translations.literal: Huai'en left the Uyghur khan encamped at Heyang and sent his son Chang, right-wing army commander, and Beiting-Shuofang army commander Gao Fucheng with more than ten thousand infantry to pursue northward on the momentum of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en left the Uyghur khan encamped at Heyang and sent his son Chang, commander of the right wing, and Gao Fucheng, Beiting-Shuofang army commander, with more than ten thousand foot soldiers in hot pursuit.

sentences.zh: 懷恩常壓賊而行，至於鄭州，再戰皆捷；

translations.literal: Huai'en constantly pressed the rebels as he marched, reaching Zheng Prefecture, where he fought twice and won each time.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en kept pressing the enemy as he marched, and at Zhengzhou won two battles in succession.

sentences.zh: 進至汴州，偽節度張獻誠開門降；

translations.literal: Advancing to Bian Prefecture, the rebel military governor Zhang Xiancheng opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Bianzhou the rebel governor Zhang Xiancheng opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又拔滑州，追破朝義於衛州。

translations.literal: He also took Hua Prefecture and pursued and defeated Chaoyi at Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He took Huazhou as well and routed Chaoyi again at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 偽睢陽節度田承嗣、李進超、李達盧等兵馬四萬餘眾，又與朝義合，據河來拒。

translations.literal: The rebel Suoyang military governor Tian Chengsi, Li Jinchao, Li Dalu, and others with more than forty thousand troops again joined Chaoyi and held the river to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel governors Tian Chengsi of Suoyang, Li Jinchao, and Li Dalu mustered more than forty thousand men, joined Chaoyi, and barred the river to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 瑒連盤濟師，登岸薄之，賊黨悉奔，長驅至昌縣東。

translations.literal: Chang repeatedly crossed the river with his army, landed on the bank, and pressed them closely. The rebel party all fled, and he drove in long pursuit to the east of Chang County.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ferried his troops across again and again, landed, and closed with the enemy. The rebels broke and ran, and he drove hard as far as the east of Chang County.

sentences.zh: 朝義率魏州兵馬來戰，又敗走，達盧來降，賊徒震駭。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led Weizhou troops to give battle and was again defeated and fled. Dalu came to surrender, and the rebel followers were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi led the Weizhou army into battle and was beaten back again. Dalu surrendered, and the rebel ranks were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 於是相州偽節度薛嵩以相、衛州、洺、邢、趙降於李抱玉、高輔成、尚文悊；

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebel Xiang military governor Xue Song surrendered Xiang, Wei, Ming, Xing, and Zhao to Li Baoyu, Gao Fucheng, and Shang Wenqi.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rebel governor Xue Song of Xiangzhou surrendered Xiang, Wei, Ming, Xing, and Zhao to Li Baoyu, Gao Fucheng, and Shang Wenqi.

sentences.zh: 偽恆陽節度李寶臣以深、恆、定、易四州降於河東節度辛雲京。

translations.literal: The rebel Hengyang military governor Li Baochen surrendered the four prefectures of Shen, Heng, Ding, and Yi to Hedong military governor Xin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel governor Li Baochen of Hengyang surrendered Shen, Heng, Ding, and Yi to Xin Yunjing, governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 朝義至貝州，又與偽大將薛忠義兩節度合。

translations.literal: Chaoyi reached Bei Prefecture and again joined forces with the rebel great general Xue Zhongyi's two military commands.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi reached Beizhou and united with the rebel general Xue Zhongyi and his two commands.

sentences.zh: 瑒至臨清，懼賊氣盛，駐軍以俟變。

translations.literal: Chang reached Linqing, feared the rebels' morale was strong, and halted his army to await a change in circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Chang reached Linqing but, seeing the rebels still full of fight, held his army in camp to wait for a turn in fortune.

sentences.zh: 朝義領眾三萬並攻具來攻，瑒令高彥崇、渾日進、李光逸等設三伏以待之，賊半渡，伏發，合擊而走之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi led thirty thousand men with siege engines to attack. Chang ordered Gao Yanchong, Hun Rijin, Li Guangyi, and others to set three ambushes to await them. When the rebels were half across, the ambush was sprung and a combined attack drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi attacked with thirty thousand men and siege equipment. Chang set Gao Yanchong, Hun Rijin, and Li Guangyi in three ambushes. When the rebels were halfway across, the trap was sprung and a combined assault sent them fleeing.

sentences.zh: 其時回紇又至，官軍益振，瑒卷甲馳之，大戰於下博縣東南。

translations.literal: At that time the Uyghurs arrived again and the government army's spirit rose still higher. Chang rolled up his armor and galloped after them, fighting a great battle southeast of Xiabo County.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs arrived again, and the imperial army's spirits soared. Chang threw off his armor for speed and gave chase, fighting a major battle southeast of Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 賊背水而陣，大軍沖擊而崩之，積屍擁流而下。

translations.literal: The rebels drew up with their backs to the water. The main army charged and broke them; corpses piled up and were borne downstream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels formed with their backs to the river. A mass charge broke their line, and corpses piled up until the current could barely pass.

sentences.zh: 朝義又走莫州。

translations.literal: Chaoyi again fled to Mo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi fled again to Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 於是河南副元帥都知兵馬使薛兼訓、兵馬使郝廷玉、兗鄆節度使辛雲京會師於下博，進軍莫州城下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Henan deputy commander-in-chief and director of army affairs Xue Jianxun, army commander Hao Tingyu, and Yan-Yun military governor Xin Yunjing united their forces at Xiabo and advanced to the walls of Mo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jianxun, director of armies under the Henan deputy commander, Hao Tingyu, army commander, and Xin Yunjing, governor of Yan and Yun, joined forces at Xiabo and marched to the walls of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義與田承嗣頻出挑戰，大敗而旋，臨陣殺其偽尚書敬榮。

translations.literal: Chaoyi and Tian Chengsi repeatedly came out to offer challenge, were thoroughly defeated and withdrew, and in the midst of battle killed their rebel Minister of Works Jing Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi and Tian Chengsi sallied out again and again, were beaten back each time, and in one engagement killed their own rebel minister Jing Rong on the field.

sentences.zh: 朝義懼，自分萬餘眾投歸義縣，留承嗣守城。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was afraid and himself led more than ten thousand men toward Guiyi County, leaving Chengsi to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chaoyi took more than ten thousand men and fled toward Guiyi County, leaving Chengsi to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 於是淄青節度侯希逸繼諸將同為攻守，凡月餘日。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zi-Qing military governor Hou Xiyi followed the other generals in joint attack and defense for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi of Zi and Qing joined the other generals in the siege, which lasted more than a month.

sentences.zh: 瑒與高彥崇、侯殺逸、薛兼訓等以眾三萬追及朝義於歸義縣，交鋒而賊潰。

translations.literal: Chang with Gao Yanchong, Hou Xiyi, Xue Jianxun, and others with thirty thousand men overtook Chaoyi at Guiyi County. They joined battle and the rebels collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, Gao Yanchong, Hou Xiyi, and Xue Jianxun overtook Chaoyi at Guiyi with thirty thousand men. A sharp engagement broke the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 屬幽州節度使李懷仙送降款，瑒頓兵於其境，遣懷仙分兵追躡。

translations.literal: Just then Youzhou military governor Li Huaixian sent in his surrender. Chang halted his army in that territory and dispatched Huaixian with divided forces in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaixian of Youzhou then submitted his surrender. Chang halted within his territory and sent Huaixian with detachments in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，朝義至平州石城縣溫泉柵，窮蹙，走入長林自縊，懷仙使妻弟徐有濟傳其首以獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year Chaoyi reached the Hot Springs stockade in Shicheng County, Ping Prefecture. Hard pressed, he went into a long grove and hanged himself. Huaixian had his wife's younger brother Xu Youji convey the head to present it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 763 Chaoyi reached the Hot Springs stockade at Shicheng in Pingzhou. Cornered, he went into a grove and hanged himself. Huaixian had his brother-in-law Xu Youji bring the head to court.

sentences.zh: 又降田承嗣之軍，河北悉平，懷恩乃與諸將班師。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi's army also surrendered, and all of Hebei was pacified. Huai'en thereupon withdrew the army with the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi's force surrendered as well, and all of Hebei was pacified. Huai'en then led the generals home.

sentences.zh: 先是，去冬郭子儀以懷恩有平定河朔之功，讓位於懷恩，遂授河北副元帥、尚書左僕射、兼中書令、靈州大都督府長史、單于鎮北大都護、朔方節度使，仍加實封四百戶，通前一千戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, the previous winter Guo Ziyi, because Huai'en had the achievement of pacifying Heshuo, yielded his post to Huai'en. He was thereupon appointed deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Grand Councilor, chief administrator of Lingzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, Chanyu Protector-General of the North, and Shuofang military governor, with an additional actual fief of four hundred households, making one thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: The winter before, Guo Ziyi had yielded his command to Huai'en in recognition of his pacification of Heshuo. Huai'en was made deputy commander of Hebei, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Grand Councilor, chief administrator of Lingzhou, Chanyu Protector-General of the North, and governor of Shuofang, with an added fief of four hundred households for a total of one thousand.

sentences.zh: 春，又加太子少師，充朔方都知兵馬使、同節度副大使，食實封五百戶，莊宅各一所，仍與一子五品官。

translations.literal: In spring he was further made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, appointed director of Shuofang army affairs and concurrent deputy military governor, with an actual fief of five hundred households, one manor and one residence each, and one son granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: That spring he was further made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, director of Shuofang armies, and concurrent deputy governor, with a fief of five hundred households, a manor and a residence, and a fifth-rank office for one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 高輔成太子少傅、兼御史中丞，充河北副元帥都知兵馬使，加實封三百戶，仍與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Gao Fucheng was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, appointed director of army affairs under the Hebei deputy commander-in-chief, with an additional actual fief of three hundred households and one son granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fucheng was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Censor-in-Chief, director of armies under the Hebei deputy commander, with a fief of three hundred households and a fifth-rank office for one son.

sentences.zh: 高彥崇太子賓客，仍舊朔方右廂兵馬使，實封二百戶，莊宅各賜一所，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Gao Yanchong was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, retaining his post as Shuofang right-wing army commander, with an actual fief of two hundred households, one manor and one residence each bestowed, and one son granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanchong was made Guest of the Heir Apparent while keeping his post as commander of the Shuofang right wing, with a fief of two hundred households, a manor and a residence, and a fifth-rank office for one son.

sentences.zh: 遂詔懷恩統可汗還蕃，遂自相州西郭口趣潞州，與回紇可汗會，出太原之北。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Huai'en to escort the khan back to his barbarian lands. He proceeded from the western outskirts of Xiang Prefecture toward Lu Prefecture to meet the Uyghur khan and went out north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Huai'en to escort the khan home. He marched from the west gate of Xiangzhou toward Luzhou to meet the Uyghur khan and led the column out north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 懷恩初至太原，辛雲京以可汗是其子婿，疑其召戎，閉關不報，且懼可汗相襲，不敢犒軍；

translations.literal: When Huai'en first reached Taiyuan, Xin Yunjing, because the khan was his son-in-law, suspected that he had summoned barbarian troops. He closed the passes and made no report, and fearing the khan might attack him as well, did not dare entertain the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en first reached Taiyuan, Xin Yunjing—whose son-in-law was the khan—suspected he had brought barbarian troops against the city. Xin shut the passes, sent no greeting, and, fearing an attack by the khan, refused to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 及還，亦如之。

translations.literal: On the return journey it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he treated them the same way.

sentences.zh: 懷恩父子宣力王室，攻城野戰，無役不從，一舉滅史朝義，復燕、趙、韓、魏之地，自以為功無以讓。

translations.literal: Huai'en father and son had proclaimed their strength for the royal house, storming cities and fighting in the field, following in no campaign they were not part of. In one stroke they destroyed Shi Chaoyi and recovered the lands of Yan, Zhao, Han, and Wei. They considered that no one else's achievements could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and his sons had poured their strength into the dynasty's cause, fighting in every campaign, storming every city. In one stroke they had destroyed Shi Chaoyi and recovered Yan, Zhao, Han, and Wei. They believed no one else's merit could match theirs.

sentences.zh: 至是，又為雲京所拒，懷恩怒，上表列其狀，頓軍汾州。

translations.literal: Now they were again rejected by Yunjing. Huai'en was angry, submitted a memorial detailing the circumstances, and halted his army at Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yunjing had snubbed them again. Huai'en was furious, memorialized the court with a full account, and halted his army at Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 會中官駱奉先使於雲京，雲京言懷恩與可汗為約，逆狀已露，乃與奉先厚結歡。

translations.literal: It happened that the eunuch Luo Fengxian was on mission to Yunjing. Yunjing said Huai'en had made a pact with the khan and that signs of rebellion were already exposed, and thereupon formed a deep bond of friendship with Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Luo Fengxian happened to be on mission to Yunjing, who told him that Huai'en had conspired with the khan and that treason was already plain. Yunjing and Fengxian then became close allies.

sentences.zh: 奉先回至懷恩所，其母數讓奉先曰：「爾等與我兒約為兄弟，今又親雲京，何兩面乎？

translations.literal: When Fengxian returned to Huai'en's camp, his mother repeatedly reproached Fengxian, saying: "You pledged brotherhood with my son, yet now you side with Yunjing—why this double face?
translations.idiomatic: When Fengxian returned to Huai'en's camp, Huai'en's mother rebuked him repeatedly: "You swore brotherhood with my son, yet now you cozy up to Yunjing—how can you face two ways at once?

sentences.zh: 雖然，前事勿諭，自今母子兄弟如初。」

translations.literal: Nevertheless, let past matters go unmentioned; from now on mother and son and brothers shall be as before."
translations.idiomatic: Still, let what is past be past; from tonight we are mother and son and brothers again."

sentences.zh: 酒酣，懷恩起舞，奉先贈纏頭彩。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep, Huai'en danced and Fengxian presented him with head-wrap silks as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Huai'en danced, and Fengxian gave him silks as a gift.

sentences.zh: 懷恩將酬其貺，奉先遽告發，懷恩曰：「明日端午，請宿為令節。」

translations.literal: Huai'en was about to return the courtesy when Fengxian suddenly denounced him. Huai'en said: "Tomorrow is the Dragon Boat Festival—please stay as my guest for the holiday."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was about to return the gift when Fengxian suddenly denounced him. Huai'en said, "Tomorrow is the Dragon Boat Festival—stay as my guest for the holiday."

sentences.zh: 奉先固辭，懷恩苦邀之，命藏其馬。

translations.literal: Fengxian firmly declined, but Huai'en pressed him insistently and ordered his horse hidden away.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian refused firmly, but Huai'en pressed him hard and had his horse hidden away.

sentences.zh: 中夕謂其從者曰：「向者責吾，又收吾馬，是將害我也。」

translations.literal: At midnight he said to his attendants: "Just now he reproached me and also took my horse—he intends to harm me."
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he told his attendants, "He scolded me earlier and took my horse—he means to kill me."

sentences.zh: 奉先懼，遂逾垣而走。

translations.literal: Fengxian was afraid and thereupon climbed over the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Fengxian climbed the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 懷恩驚，遽令追還其馬。

translations.literal: Huai'en was alarmed and at once ordered his horse pursued and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was startled and immediately sent men to return his horse.

sentences.zh: 奉先使回，奏其反狀。

translations.literal: Fengxian sent back his messenger and reported signs of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian sent word back to court reporting treason.

sentences.zh: 懷恩累奏請誅雲京、奉先，上以雲京有功，手詔和解之，懷恩遂有貳於我。

translations.literal: Huai'en repeatedly memorialized requesting execution of Yunjing and Fengxian. The emperor, because Yunjing had merit, sent a personal edict to reconcile them. Huai'en thereupon became disloyal to us.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en repeatedly asked the throne to execute Yunjing and Fengxian. The emperor, citing Yunjing's service, sent a personal edict urging reconciliation. From that point Huai'en turned against the court.

sentences.zh: 至七月，改元廣德，冊勛拜太保，仍與一子三品、一子四品官並階，仍加實封五百戶。

translations.literal: By the seventh month the era name was changed to Guangde. He was enfeoffed for merit and appointed Grand Mentor, with one son granted a third-rank office and one son a fourth-rank office each advanced a step, and an additional actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the era was renamed Guangde. Huai'en was honored for merit and made Grand Mentor, with one son given a third-rank post and another a fourth-rank post, each advanced one step, plus an added fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仆固瑒一子五品官，加實封一百戶。

translations.literal: Pugu Chang was granted a fifth-rank office for one son and an additional actual fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was given a fifth-rank office for one of his sons and an added fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍賜鐵券，以名藏太廟，畫像於淩煙閣。

translations.literal: He was further granted an iron certificate, his name deposited in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and his portrait painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He also received an iron certificate of immunity, had his name recorded in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and his portrait hung in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 尋以瑒為御史大夫、朔方行營節度。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Chang was appointed Censor-in-Chief and military governor of the Shuofang field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Chang was made Censor-in-Chief and governor of the Shuofang field command.

sentences.zh: 懷恩以寇難已來，一門之內死王事者四十六人，女嫁絕域，再收兩京，皆導引回紇，摧滅強敵，而為人媒孽，蕃性獷戾，怏怏不已。

translations.literal: Huai'en, since the troubles of invasion had begun, had forty-six within his clan die in the king's service. His daughters were married to distant lands. Twice he recovered the two capitals, each time guiding the Uyghurs and crushing powerful enemies—yet he was made the object of slander. His barbarian nature was fierce and obstinate, and he was discontented without end.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellion began, forty-six members of Huai'en's clan had died in imperial service. His daughters had been married into distant lands. He had twice recovered the two capitals, each time leading the Uyghurs to crush the enemy—yet he was slandered at court. Fierce by birth and increasingly bitter, he could not find peace.

sentences.zh: 乃上書自敘功伐，曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial recounting his achievements, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the throne with an account of his deeds, writing:

sentences.zh: 廣德元年八月二十三日，開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、兼中書令、朔方節度副大使、河北副元帥、上柱國、大寧郡王臣懷恩，刺肝瀝血，謹頓首頓首上書寶應聖文神武皇帝陛下：臣家本蕃夷，代居邊塞，爰自祖父，早沐國恩。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of the eighth month of the first year of Guangde, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with independent office, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Grand Councilor, Shuofang deputy military governor, Hebei deputy commander-in-chief, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Daning, your subject Huai'en, having pierced my liver and drained my blood, bow my head again and again in submitting this memorial to Your Majesty the Baoying Sage, Literate, Divine, and Martial Emperor: My family is originally of barbarian stock, dwelling for generations on the frontier. From my grandfather's time we have long bathed in the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-third day of the eighth month, first year of Guangde: Huai'en, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Vice Director, concurrent Grand Councilor, deputy governor of Shuofang, deputy commander of Hebei, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Daning, bows in blood and tears before Your Majesty the Baoying Sage Emperor: My family is of frontier origin, settled on the border for generations. From my grandfather onward we have lived under the dynasty's grace.

sentences.zh: 臣年未弱冠，即蒙上皇驅策，出入死生，竭力疆場，叨承先帝報功，時年已授特進。

translations.literal: Before I had reached twenty I was already driven forth by the Retired Emperor, passing in and out of life and death and exerting my strength on the battlefield. I was favored with the former emperor's reward for achievement and at that time was already granted special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Before I was twenty the Retired Emperor sent me into battle. I faced death again and again and gave everything on the frontier. The former emperor rewarded my service, and I was granted special advancement while still young.

sentences.zh: 洎乎祿山作亂，大振王師，臣累任偏裨，決死靖難，上以安社稷，下以拯生靈，仗皇天之威神，滅狂胡之醜類。

translations.literal: When Lushan rose in rebellion and the royal army was greatly roused, I repeatedly held subordinate commands, resolved to die in quelling the turmoil—above to secure the altars of state, below to rescue the living masses—relying on Heaven's awesome spirit to destroy the mad barbarian rabble.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled and the imperial armies marched, I served again and again as a subordinate commander, ready to die to restore order—above, to save the dynasty; below, to rescue the people—trusting in Heaven's power to destroy the rebel horde.

sentences.zh: 無何，思明繼逆，又據東周，宸極不安，海內騰沸。

translations.literal: Before long Siming followed in rebellion and again seized the Eastern Zhou. The imperial seat was unsettled and the realm seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Siming followed in revolt and seized the eastern heartland. The throne trembled and the empire boiled with unrest.

sentences.zh: 臣謬承大行皇帝委任，授以兵權，誓雪國仇，以匡時難。

translations.literal: I was undeservedly entrusted by the late emperor with command and granted military authority, swearing to wipe away the nation's enmity and rectify the crisis of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor wrongly entrusted me with command and gave me authority over the armies, swearing to avenge the dynasty and set the realm right.

sentences.zh: 闔門忠烈，咸願殺身，野戰攻城，皆先士卒。

translations.literal: The whole household was loyal and fierce; all were willing to give their lives. In field battles and storming cities we were always ahead of the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: My whole clan was loyal to the death. In every battle and siege we led from the front.

sentences.zh: 兄弟死於陣敵，子侄沒於軍前，九族之親，十不存一，縱有在者，瘡痍遍身。

translations.literal: Brothers died before the enemy lines; sons and nephews perished before the army. Of the nine degrees of kinship, not one in ten survived; even those who remained were covered with wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers fell on the battlefield; sons and nephews died before the ranks. Of my extended family, fewer than one in ten survived, and those who lived were scarred head to foot.

sentences.zh: 況陛下潛龍之時，親統師旅，臣忝事麾下，陛下悉臣愚誠。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty was still a hidden dragon and personally commanded the armies, I was honored to serve under your banner, and Your Majesty knew my simple loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was still heir and led the armies in person, I served under your banner, and you knew my simple loyalty.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝未捐宮館之時，臣頻立微效，累沾官賞，遂被輔國等讒害，幾至破家，便奪兵權，逾年宿衛。

translations.literal: Before the late emperor departed the palace halls I repeatedly achieved small merit and was repeatedly touched by official rewards, but then I was slandered by Fuguo and others, nearly to the ruin of my house. My military authority was at once taken away, and for more than a year I served in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before the late emperor died I won merit again and again and received repeated honors, but Li Fuguo and others slandered me nearly to the destruction of my house. My command was stripped away, and for more than a year I served as a palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 臣雖內省無疚，終懼讒佞傾危，以日繼時，命懸秋葉，至將歸骨泉壤，永謝明時。

translations.literal: Though inwardly I found no fault, I still feared that slanderers and flatterers would overturn me. Day followed day and my life hung like an autumn leaf, until I was about to return my bones to the yellow springs and bid the bright age farewell forever.
translations.idiomatic: Though I knew myself innocent, I feared slander would destroy me. Day by day my life hung by a thread, until I expected to die in obscurity and never see the light again.

sentences.zh: 幸遇陛下龍躍天衢，繼纘鴻業，知臣負謗，察臣丹心，遂開獨見之明，杜絕眾多之口，特拔臣於汧、隴，再任臣於朔方。

translations.literal: Fortunately I encountered Your Majesty's dragon leap upon the heavenly path and succession to the great enterprise. Knowing that I bore calumny, discerning my loyal heart, you opened your unique insight and shut the mouths of the many, specially raising me from Qian and Long and again appointing me in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune brought Your Majesty to the throne. You knew I had been slandered and saw my loyal heart. You silenced my accusers, raised me from Qian and Long, and entrusted me with Shuofang once more.

sentences.zh: 誠謂遊魂返骸，枯骨再肉，使臣得竭駑蹇之力，效錐刀之功，上答陛下再造之恩，下展微臣犬馬之志。

translations.literal: I truly believed that a wandering soul had returned to its frame and dry bones had put on flesh again, enabling me to exhaust the strength of a worn nag and render the service of a knife's edge—above to repay Your Majesty's grace of second birth, below to display this humble subject's will to serve like dog or horse.
translations.idiomatic: I thought my soul had returned to my body and my dry bones had flesh again. I would give my last strength, however slight, to repay your grace of restoration and prove my devotion as your humble servant.

sentences.zh: 去年秋末，回紇伏義而來，士庶不知，悉皆驚駭。

translations.literal: At the end of last autumn the Uyghurs came in righteous allegiance. The officials and common people did not understand and were all alarmed and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Late last autumn the Uyghurs came in alliance, and the people, not understanding, were terrified.

sentences.zh: 陛下以臣與其姻婭，令至太原祗迎，一切事宜，許臣逐便處置。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because I was related by marriage to them, ordered me to Taiyuan to receive them with respect. All matters were permitted to be handled by me as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Because I was related to them by marriage, Your Majesty sent me to Taiyuan to welcome them and authorized me to handle all arrangements as I saw fit.

sentences.zh: 遂與可汗計議，分道用兵，克復洛陽，平蕩幽、薊，惟有神策兵馬，頓軍獨住陳留。

translations.literal: I then deliberated with the khan and divided our forces. We recovered Luoyang and pacified You and Ji. Only the Shence troops halted their army alone at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: I consulted with the khan and divided our forces, retook Luoyang, and pacified You and Ji, while the Shence army alone held Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 可汗時在洛陽，即被朝恩猜阻，要為流議，已失蕃情。

translations.literal: The khan was then at Luoyang and was at once subjected to Chao'en's suspicion and obstruction, becoming the target of loose talk and already losing the barbarians' goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was then at Luoyang, where Yu Chao'en's suspicion and obstruction turned rumor against him and alienated the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 臣自平賊卻回，天恩又令餞送，臣遂罄竭家產，為國周旋，發遣外蕃，貴圖上道。

translations.literal: After I returned from pacifying the rebels, Heaven's grace again ordered a farewell feast and escort. I thereupon exhausted my household property in circling on the state's behalf to dispatch the outer barbarians, valuing the plan of sending them homeward.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the rebels I was ordered to escort the allies home. I exhausted my household wealth to see them off properly and send them on their way.

sentences.zh: 行至山北，被奉先、雲京共生異見，妄作加諸，閉城不出祗迎，仍令潛行竊盜。

translations.literal: When I reached north of the mountains I was jointly given strange views by Fengxian and Yunjing, who falsely laid charges against me, closed their cities and did not come out to receive me with respect, and even ordered secret raids and theft.
translations.idiomatic: North of the mountains, Fengxian and Yunjing turned against me with false accusations, shut their gates instead of welcoming me, and even sent men to steal from my camp.

sentences.zh: 蕃夷怨怒，早欲相仇，臣遂彌縫，方得出界。

translations.literal: The barbarians were angry and resentful and long wished to take revenge on one another. I then patched matters over before they could leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: The nomad allies were furious and nearly came to blows. Only my mediation got them across the border in peace.

sentences.zh: 及其祖餞事了，回至太原，臣忝跡鼎司，又承重寄，奉先、雲京曾無禮數，閉關不出相看。

translations.literal: When the farewell rites were finished and I returned to Taiyuan, I was honored to stand in the highest offices and again bore heavy trust. Fengxian and Yunjing showed no courtesy at all, closing the passes and not coming out to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the farewell ceremonies were done and I returned to Taiyuan, I held high office and heavy responsibility. Yet Fengxian and Yunjing showed no courtesy, shutting their gates and refusing even to receive me.

sentences.zh: 臣遂過汾州，休息士馬，凡經數日，不遣一介知聞。

translations.literal: I thereupon passed Fen Prefecture to rest troops and horses. Several days passed without sending a single messenger to inform them.
translations.idiomatic: I passed through Fenzhou to rest my troops for several days without sending them so much as a message.

sentences.zh: 自以行事乘疏，恐臣先有論奏，遂乃構其謗黷，妄起異端，扇動軍城，以為設備。

translations.literal: They considered their conduct negligent and feared I had already submitted accusations, and so fabricated slander and irreverence, groundlessly raising sedition and stirring the garrison cities as if making preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling guilty and fearing I had already memorialized against them, they fabricated charges of sedition and stirred the garrisons as though I were preparing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又臣從潞府過日，見抱玉只迎回紇，庶事用心，懇稱家資罄於公用，又與臣馬兼銀器四事，臣於回紇處得絹，便與抱玉二千匹以充答贈。

translations.literal: Moreover, when I passed through Lu Prefecture I saw Baoyu receiving only the Uyghurs with full attention to every matter, earnestly saying his household wealth was exhausted for public use. He also gave me horses and four kinds of silver vessels. I obtained silk from the Uyghurs and at once gave Baoyu two thousand bolts in return for his gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Luzhou I saw Baoyu lavishing attention on the Uyghur reception and claiming his family fortune was spent for the state. He gave me horses and silver vessels. I obtained silk from the Uyghurs and gave Baoyu two thousand bolts in return.

sentences.zh: 今被抱玉共相組織，將此往來之貺，便為結托之私，貴在厚誣，務相傾奪。

translations.literal: Now I am jointly framed by Baoyu, who turns these exchanges of gifts into evidence of private collusion, valuing heavy slander and striving to overthrow and seize from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Now Baoyu has joined the plot, turning these courtesies into evidence of conspiracy, heaping slander upon me to bring me down.

sentences.zh: 陛下不垂明察，采聽流言，欲令忠直之臣，枉陷讒邪之黨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not bestow clear scrutiny but listens to loose talk, wishing to make a loyal and upright minister fall wrongly into the party of slanderers and villains.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not investigate but listens to rumor, allowing loyal men to be destroyed by slanderers.

sentences.zh: 臣實不欺天地，不負神明，夙夜三思，臣罪有六：

translations.literal: I truly do not deceive Heaven and Earth or fail the spirits. Night and day I reflect three times: I have six crimes:
translations.idiomatic: I have not deceived Heaven or Earth or failed the spirits. Night and day I ask myself, and I find six crimes:

sentences.zh: 往年同羅背叛，河曲騷然，經略數軍，兵圍不解。

translations.literal: In years past the Tongluo rebelled and the Hequ region was disturbed. Several frontier armies were encircled without relief.
translations.idiomatic: Years ago the Tongluo rebelled and the Hequ frontier was in turmoil. Several armies were besieged without relief.

sentences.zh: 臣不顧老母，走投靈州，先帝嘉臣忠誠，遂遣征兵討叛，使得河曲清泰，賊徒奔亡。

translations.literal: Disregarding my aged mother, I fled posthaste to Ling Prefecture. The former emperor praised my loyalty and thereupon sent troops to attack the rebels, enabling the Hequ to become clear and peaceful and the rebel band to flee in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: I left my aged mother and raced to Lingzhou. The former emperor praised my loyalty and sent troops to crush the rebellion, restoring peace to the Hequ and driving the rebels to flight.

sentences.zh: 是臣不忠於國，其罪一也。

translations.literal: This is my disloyalty to the state—my first crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣男玢嘗被同羅虜將，蓋亦制不由己，旋即棄逆歸順，卻來投臣，臣斬之以令士眾。

translations.literal: My son Bin was once captured by Tongluo raiders—he too was not master of his own actions—and shortly abandoned rebellion and returned to loyalty, then came to join me. I executed him to command the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: My son Bin was once captured by the Tongluo, then escaped and came back to me. I executed him to uphold discipline in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 且臣不愛骨肉之重，而徇忠義之誠，是臣不忠於國，其罪二也。

translations.literal: Moreover, I did not cherish the weight of flesh and blood but followed the sincerity of loyalty and righteousness. This is my disloyalty to the state—my second crime.
translations.idiomatic: I valued loyalty above kinship. This is my second crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣有二女，俱聘遠蕃，為國和親，合從討難，致使賊徒殄滅。

translations.literal: I have two daughters, both betrothed to distant barbarians for the state's marriage alliances, joining forces to attack the crisis and thereby causing the rebel band to be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: I gave two daughters in marriage to distant allies to secure the realm, and together we destroyed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 寰宇清平。

translations.literal: The realm was clear and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at peace.

sentences.zh: 是臣不忠於國，其罪三也。

translations.literal: This is my disloyalty to the state—my third crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is my third crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣及男瑒，不顧危亡，身先行陣，父子效命，志寧邦家。

translations.literal: I and my son Chang, heedless of peril and death, personally led the van. Father and son gave their lives in service with the will to pacify state and family.
translations.idiomatic: My son Chang and I, heedless of death, led from the front. Father and son risked everything to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 是臣不忠於國，其罪四也。

translations.literal: This is my disloyalty to the state—my fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fourth crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下委臣副元帥之權，令臣指麾河北。

translations.literal: Your Majesty entrusted me with the authority of deputy commander-in-chief and ordered me to command Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty made me deputy commander and placed Hebei under my command.

sentences.zh: 其新附節度使，皆握強兵，臣之撫綏，悉安反側，州縣既定，賦稅以時。

translations.literal: The newly submitted military governors all held powerful armies. Through my soothing governance all were settled in their wavering, prefectures and counties were stabilized, and taxes were delivered on time.
translations.idiomatic: The newly submitted governors all held strong armies. I pacified them all, restored order to the prefectures and counties, and taxes flowed on schedule.

sentences.zh: 是臣不忠於國，其罪五也。

translations.literal: This is my disloyalty to the state—my fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fifth crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣葉和回紇，戡定凶徒，天下削平，蕃夷歸國，使其永為鄰好。

translations.literal: I reconciled with the Uyghurs, quelled the vicious rebels, leveled the realm, and sent the barbarians home, causing them to be forever good neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: I reconciled with the Uyghurs, crushed the rebels, pacified the realm, and sent the allies home as lasting neighbors.

sentences.zh: 義著急難，萬姓安寧，干戈止息，二聖山陵事畢，陛下忠孝兩全。

translations.literal: Righteousness was shown in urgent crisis, the myriad people were secure, arms ceased, the tombs of the two sages were completed, and Your Majesty fulfilled both loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: I served in the nation's crisis, brought peace to the people, ended the fighting, and helped complete the tombs of the two emperors so that Your Majesty could fulfill both loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 是臣不忠於國，其罪六也。

translations.literal: This is my disloyalty to the state—my sixth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is my sixth crime of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣既負六罪，誠合萬誅，延頸轅門，以待斧鑕。

translations.literal: Since I bear these six crimes, I truly deserve ten thousand executions. I stretch my neck at the camp gate awaiting the axe and cleaver.
translations.idiomatic: With these six crimes I deserve death a thousand times over. I stretch my neck at the camp gate and await the executioner's axe.

sentences.zh: 過此以往，更無他違。

translations.literal: Beyond this there is no further transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this I have done nothing wrong.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以此誅臣，何異伍子胥存吳，卒浮屍於江上，大夫種霸越，終賜劍於稽山。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty executes me for this, how is it different from Wu Zixu preserving Wu yet in the end floating as a corpse on the river, or Grandee Zhong dominating Yue yet in the end receiving the sword at Kuaiji Mountain?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty kills me for this, what difference is there from Wu Zixu, who saved Wu yet ended floating on the river, or Fan Li, who made Yue supreme yet was given the sword at Kuaiji?

sentences.zh: 唯當吞恨九泉，銜冤千古，復何訴哉！

translations.literal: I can only swallow my resentment in the nine springs and bear injustice for a thousand ages—what further appeal is there!
translations.idiomatic: I can only swallow my grief in the grave and bear injustice for ages—to whom can I appeal!

sentences.zh: 復何訴哉！

translations.literal: What further appeal is there!
translations.idiomatic: To whom can I appeal!

sentences.zh: 且葵藿尚解仰陽，犬馬猶能戀主，臣忝恩至重，委任非輕，夙夜思奉天顏，豈暫心離魏闕，誠恐以忠獲罪，龜鏡不遙。

translations.literal: Moreover, even sunflowers understand turning toward the sun, and dogs and horses can still love their master. I am honored with grace of the utmost weight and entrusted with responsibility not light. Night and day I think of beholding the imperial countenance—how could my heart for a moment leave the Wei gate? I truly fear receiving punishment for loyalty; the tortoise mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Even sunflowers turn toward the sun, and dogs and horses love their master. Your grace to me is boundless and your trust weighty. Night and day I long to see your face—how could I leave the court even for a moment? I fear only that loyalty will be punished, as history shows all too clearly.

sentences.zh: 頃者來瑱受誅，朝廷不示其罪，天下忠義，從此生疑。

translations.literal: Recently Lai Tian was executed, yet the court did not show his crime. Loyal and righteous men throughout the realm from this sprang doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian was recently executed without the court stating his crime, and loyal men everywhere began to doubt.

sentences.zh: 況來瑱功業素高，人多所忌，不審聖衷獨斷，復為奸臣弄權？

translations.literal: Moreover, Lai Tian's achievements were always lofty and many envied him. Was it not clear whether the sacred mind decided alone, or whether villainous ministers again manipulated power?
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian's achievements were great and many envied him. Did Your Majesty decide alone, or did wicked ministers manipulate power again?

sentences.zh: 臣欲入朝，恐罹斯禍，諸道節度使皆懼，非臣獨敢如此。

translations.literal: I wish to enter court but fear falling into this calamity. Military governors of every circuit are all afraid—not I alone dare to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to come to court but fear this fate. Every regional governor is afraid—not I alone.

sentences.zh: 近聞追詔數人，並皆不至，實畏中官讒口，又懼陛下損傷，豈唯是臣不忠，只為回邪在側。

translations.literal: Recently I heard that several men summoned by edict all failed to come. They truly fear the slanderous mouths of inner eunuchs and also fear harm to Your Majesty. How is it only that I am disloyal? It is only because perverse villains are at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Several men recently summoned by edict failed to come. They fear the eunuchs' slander and harm to Your Majesty. It is not I alone who hesitate—it is because villains stand at your side.

sentences.zh: 且臣前後所奏駱奉先詞情，非不摭實，陛下竟無處置，寵用彌深。

translations.literal: Moreover, the wording of my memorials before and after regarding Luo Fengxian was not without basis in fact, yet Your Majesty made no disposition and favored and employed him ever more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: My memorials against Luo Fengxian were grounded in fact, yet Your Majesty took no action and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 皆由同類相從，致蒙蔽聖聰，人皆懼死，誰復敢言！

translations.literal: All because their kind follow one another, causing the sage intelligence to be blinded. Everyone fears death—who again dares speak!
translations.idiomatic: Their kind protect one another and blind the throne. All fear death—who dares speak!

sentences.zh: 臣義切君臣，志憂社稷，若無極諫，有負聖朝，敢肆愚忠，以幹鼎鑊。

translations.literal: My righteousness binds me to sovereign and minister; my will grieves for altars and state. If I offer no utmost remonstrance I fail the holy court. I dare unleash simple loyalty and touch the imperial cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: My duty binds me to sovereign and minister; my heart grieves for the realm. If I do not speak plainly I fail the dynasty. I dare offer blunt loyalty though it risk the imperial wrath.

sentences.zh: 況今西有犬戎背亂，東有吳、越不庭，均、房群盜縱橫，鄜、坊稽胡草擾。

translations.literal: Moreover, now in the west the Rong dogs turn their backs in rebellion; in the east Wu and Yue do not attend court; bandits run rampant in Jun and Fang; and Jiehu of Fu and Fang harass like grass.
translations.idiomatic: In the west the Rong rebel; in the east Wu and Yue defy the court; bandits roam Jun and Fang; and nomad raiders trouble Fu and Fang.

sentences.zh: 陛下不思外禦，而乃內忌忠良，何以混一車書，而使梯航納贐？

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not think of defense abroad but instead inwardly envies the loyal and good—how can you unify carriage and script and cause ladder-ships to present tribute?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thinks not of defending the borders but of destroying loyal servants within—how can the realm be unified or distant peoples bring tribute?

sentences.zh: 天下至大，豈可暫輕。

translations.literal: The realm is utmost great—how can it be lightly treated even for a moment?
translations.idiomatic: The empire is vast—how can it be treated lightly even for a moment?

sentences.zh: 伏承四方敷奏之人，引對之時，陛下皆云與驃騎商量，曾不委宰臣可否。

translations.literal: I respectfully hear that when men from the four quarters present memorials and are granted audience, Your Majesty always says you will consult the Champion General and never entrust approval or denial to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when petitioners from the provinces are received, Your Majesty always says you will consult the Champion General and never asks the chief ministers for judgment.

sentences.zh: 或有稽留數月，不放歸還，遠近之心，轉加疑阻。

translations.literal: Some are detained for months without being released to return. Hearts near and far grow ever more doubtful and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Some are detained for months without release. Mistrust spreads far and wide.

sentences.zh: 且臣朔方將士，功效最高，為先帝中興主人，是陛下蒙塵故吏，曾不別加優獎，卻信嫉妒謗詞，子儀先已被猜，臣今又遭毀黷。

translations.literal: Moreover, my Shuofang officers and soldiers have the highest achievements. We were the former emperor's masters in restoring the dynasty and are Your Majesty's old officers from the days of dust on the throne. Yet we were never specially given added rewards but instead believed jealous slander. Ziyi was first already suspected; I now again suffer defamation and insult.
translations.idiomatic: My Shuofang troops have served with the highest merit. We restored the dynasty for the late emperor and followed Your Majesty in exile. Yet we receive no special reward, only jealous slander. Guo Ziyi was suspected first; now I am defamed as well.

sentences.zh: 弓藏鳥盡，兔死犬烹，臣昔謂非，今方知實。

translations.literal: When the bow is stored the birds are spent; when the rabbit dies the dog is boiled. I once thought this untrue; now I know it is real.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow is stored the birds are gone; when the rabbit dies the hound is cooked. I once thought this a proverb only; now I know it true.

sentences.zh: 且臣息軍汾上，關鍵大開，收馬放羊，曾無守備，分兵數郡，貴免般糧，勸課農桑，務安黎庶，有何狀跡，而涉異端。

translations.literal: Moreover, I rested my army on the Fen, opened the passes wide, gathered horses and herded sheep with never a guard set up, divided troops among several commanderies to spare transport of grain, urged farming and sericulture, and strove to settle the common people—what trace of conduct touches sedition?
translations.idiomatic: I rested my army on the Fen, opened the passes, pastured horses and sheep without heavy guard, spread troops among the commanderies to ease grain transport, and urged farming to settle the people—what sign of rebellion is there in this?

sentences.zh: 陛下必信矯詞，何殊指鹿為馬？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must believe twisted words, how is it different from calling a deer a horse?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes these twisted words, what difference is there from calling a deer a horse?

sentences.zh: 陛下倘斥逐邪佞，親附忠良，蠲削狐疑，敷陳政化，使君臣無二，天下歸心，則窺邊之戎，不足為患，梗命之寇，將復何憂，偃武修文，其則不遠。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would drive out the wicked and flatterers, draw near the loyal and good, cut away doubt, and spread civilizing government so that sovereign and minister are without division and the realm turns its heart homeward, then the Rong who spy at the border are insufficient to be a trouble and the rebels who obstruct commands—what further worry? To lay down arms and cultivate culture is not far.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would cast out the wicked, embrace the loyal, clear away suspicion, and govern openly so that sovereign and ministers are united and the realm gives its heart to the throne, border raiders would be no threat and rebels nothing to fear. To lay down arms and cultivate culture would not be far off.

sentences.zh: 陛下若不納愚懇，且貴因循，臣實不敢保家，陛下豈能安國！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not accept my foolish earnestness but instead values routine and delay, I truly dare not preserve my house—how can Your Majesty secure the state!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not heed my plea but values routine instead, I cannot save my house—and how can Your Majesty secure the state!

sentences.zh: 忠言利行，良藥愈病，伏惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Loyal words benefit conduct; good medicine cures illness. I bow my head and beg Your Majesty to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words aid action; bitter medicine cures disease. I beg Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 臣今戎事已安，糧儲且繼，深願一至闕下，披露心肝，再睹聖顏，萬死無恨。

translations.literal: My military affairs are now settled and grain stores continue in succession. I deeply wish to come once to the palace gates, lay bare my heart and liver, behold the sacred countenance again, and have no regret though I die ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: My campaigns are settled and supplies hold. I long to come to court, lay bare my heart, see your face again, and die without regret.

sentences.zh: 臣欲公然進發，慮恐將士留連。

translations.literal: I wish to advance openly but fear the officers and soldiers will linger and delay.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to march openly to court but fear my troops will not follow.

sentences.zh: 臣今便托巡晉、絳等州，於彼遷延且住，謹遣押衙開府儀同三司、試太常卿張休臧先進書兼口奏事。

translations.literal: I now take the pretext of inspecting Jin, Jiang, and other prefectures and will linger and halt there. I respectfully send my yamen guard, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Xiuzang, acting chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, ahead with this letter and an oral report of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I will tour Jin, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures and remain there for a time. I send ahead my officer Zhang Xiuzang, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with this letter and an oral report.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下覽臣此書，知臣誠懇，特垂聖斷，勿議近臣，待臣如初，浮謗不入，臣當死節王命，誓酬國恩。
