translations.literal: I bow my head and beg Your Majesty to read this letter of mine, know my sincere earnestness, specially bestow sacred judgment, not deliberate with nearby ministers, treat me as at first, let floating slander not enter, and I shall die upholding the king's command and swear to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to read this letter, know my sincerity, decide for yourself without consulting those around you, treat me as before, keep slander out, and I will die upholding the throne's command and repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 仍請遣一介專使至絳州問臣，臣即便與同行，冀獲蹈舞軒陛。

translations.literal: I further request that a single dedicated envoy be sent to Jiang Prefecture to inquire of me; I will at once go together with him, hoping to obtain the joy of dancing before the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Please send a special envoy to Jiangzhou to summon me. I will come at once and hope to bow before the throne.

sentences.zh: 鄙臣愚慮，不顧死亡，輕觸天威，戰汗無地。

translations.literal: This humble subject's foolish thought, heedless of death, lightly touching Heaven's majesty—I tremble in sweat with no place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, heedless of death, has lightly touched imperial majesty and trembles without knowing where to stand.

sentences.zh: 九月，上以回紇近塞，懷恩又與辛雲京有隙，上欲其悔過，推心以待之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because the Uyghurs were near the border and Huai'en also had a rift with Xin Yunjing, the emperor wished him to repent his faults and met him with an open heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with the Uyghurs near the border and Huai'en at odds with Xin Yunjing, the emperor wished him to repent and met him with an open heart.

sentences.zh: 恐其不信，詔召黃門侍郎裴遵慶使汾州喻旨，且察其去就。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not believe, an edict summoned Yellow Gate Vice Minister Pei Zunqing as envoy to Fen Prefecture to explain the imperial intent and observe his course of action.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would not trust the court, the emperor sent Vice Minister Pei Zunqing to Fenzhou to explain the imperial intent and observe his intentions.

sentences.zh: 遵慶即至，懷恩抱其足號泣而訴，遵慶因宣聖恩優厚，諷令入朝，懷恩許諾。

translations.literal: Zunqing arrived at once. Huai'en embraced his feet, weeping and wailing in appeal. Zunqing thereupon proclaimed the sage grace as generous and kindly urged him to enter court. Huai'en promised.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing arrived. Huai'en seized his feet and wept as he pleaded his case. Zunqing proclaimed the emperor's generous grace and urged him to come to court. Huai'en agreed.

sentences.zh: 副將范志誠說之曰：「公以讒言交構，有功高不賞之懼，嫌隙已成，奈何入不測之朝？

translations.literal: Deputy general Fan Zhicheng admonished him, saying: "Sir, through slanderous words you have been framed. You have the fear of lofty achievement without reward. The rift is already formed—how can you enter a court whose outcome cannot be known?
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Fan Zhicheng warned him, "You have been framed by slander. You fear the fate of great merit unrewarded. The breach is already made—how can you enter a court whose outcome no one can know?

sentences.zh: 公不見來瑱、李光弼之事乎！

translations.literal: Have you not seen the cases of Lai Tian and Li Guangbi!
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen what happened to Lai Tian and Li Guangbi!

sentences.zh: 功成而不見容，二臣以走誅。」

translations.literal: When achievement was complete they were not tolerated; both ministers were executed for fleeing."
translations.idiomatic: When their work was done they were not tolerated; both were killed for fleeing."

sentences.zh: 懷恩然之。

translations.literal: Huai'en agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，又以懼死為辭，許令一子入朝，志誠又不可。

translations.literal: The next day he again took fear of death as his excuse and was permitted to send one son to court, but Zhicheng again would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again pleaded fear of death and offered to send one son to court instead, but Zhicheng would not allow even that.

sentences.zh: 遵慶復命。

translations.literal: Zunqing returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing returned to report.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫王翊自回紇使還，懷恩與可汗往來，恐泄其事，乃止之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Yi returned from his mission to the Uyghurs. Huai'en was in communication with the khan and, fearing the matter would be leaked, detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Yi returned from his mission to the Uyghurs. Huai'en, still in contact with the khan, feared the plot would leak and detained him.

sentences.zh: 遂令子瑒率眾攻雲京，雲京出戰，瑒大敗而旋，進圍榆次，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered his son Chang to lead troops to attack Yunjing. Yunjing came out to fight; Chang was thoroughly defeated and withdrew, then advanced to besiege Yuci. The court was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Chang to attack Yunjing. Yunjing met him in battle and routed him. Chang withdrew and besieged Yuci instead, alarming the court.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚書右丞顏真卿請奉詔懷恩，上因以真卿為刑部尚書、兼御史大夫往宣慰之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs Yan Zhenqing had requested to carry an edict to Huai'en. The emperor thereupon appointed Zhenqing Minister of Justice and concurrent Censor-in-Chief to go and console him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan Zhenqing, Right Vice Minister, had volunteered to carry an edict to Huai'en. The emperor appointed him Minister of Justice and Censor-in-Chief to go as envoy of consolation.

sentences.zh: 真卿曰：「臣往請行者，時也；

translations.literal: Zhenqing said: "When I previously requested to go, that was the time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing said, "When I asked to go before, that was the time.

sentences.zh: 今方受命，事無益矣。」

translations.literal: Now that I have just received the commission, the affair will be of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have my commission, the mission is useless."

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「懷恩阻兵，是其反側明矣。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason. He replied: "Huai'en blocks the army—his wavering and rebellion are already clear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. He replied, "Huai'en is holding his army in check—his rebellion is already plain.

sentences.zh: 頃陛下避狄於陜郊，臣方責以《春秋》之義，雲寡君蒙塵於郊，敢不恭問官守。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty recently avoided the Di at the Shaan suburbs, I was just then reproaching him with the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, saying that when a lone ruler is dust-covered in the suburbs, how dare one not respectfully inquire after the official charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was in exile at Shaan, I was reproaching him with the Spring and Autumn Annals: when the ruler is in distress in the field, how dare a subject not respectfully inquire after his charge?

sentences.zh: 當是時也，懷恩來朝，以助討賊，則其辭順。

translations.literal: At that time, Huai'en came to court to assist in punishing the rebels—then his words were deferential.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huai'en had come to court offering to help crush the rebels, and his language was perfectly deferential.

sentences.zh: 今陛下攘去犬戎，即宮京邑，懷恩進不勤王，退不釋眾，其辭曲，必不來矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has driven away the canine Rong, returned to the palace in the capital, yet Huai'en in advancing does not relieve the throne and in retreating does not dismiss his troops; his words are evasive—he surely will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has driven off the barbarians and returned to the capital, Huai'en neither marches to the emperor's aid nor disbands his army when he withdraws. His language is disingenuous—he will certainly not come.

sentences.zh: 且明懷恩反者，獨辛雲京、李抱玉、駱奉先、魚朝恩四人耳，自外朝臣，咸言其枉。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who clearly say Huai'en rebelled are only the four—Xin Yunjing, Li Baoyu, Luo Fengxian, and Yu Chao'en; apart from them, court ministers all say he is wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, only Xin Yunjing, Li Baoyu, Luo Fengxian, and Yu Chao'en openly claim Huai'en has rebelled; all other court officials insist he has been wronged.

sentences.zh: 然懷恩將士，皆子儀部曲，恩信結其心，陛下何不以子儀代之，喻以逆順禍福，必相率而歸耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Huai'en's officers and soldiers are all Ziyi's retainers; favor and trust bind their hearts. Why does Your Majesty not send Ziyi in his place, instruct them on rebellion and loyalty, fortune and disaster—they will surely follow one another back."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huai'en's troops all served under Guo Ziyi and remain bound to him by personal loyalty. Your Majesty should send Guo Ziyi to replace him and explain the consequences of rebellion versus obedience—they will surely return in succession."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 子儀至河中，仆固瑒已為朔方兵馬使張惟嶽等四人斬其首，獻於闕下。

translations.literal: When Ziyi reached Hedong, Pugu Chang had already been beheaded by the four including Zhang Weiyue, Shuofang army and cavalry commissioner; his head was presented at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Guo Ziyi reached Hedong, Pugu Chang had already been beheaded by Zhang Weiyue and three other Shuofang officers, and his head sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 懷恩聞之，率麾下數百騎，棄其母，渡河北走靈武。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Huai'en led several hundred horsemen of his command, abandoned his mother, crossed north of the river, and fled to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en learned of this, he took a few hundred horsemen, abandoned his mother, crossed north of the Yellow River, and fled toward Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 余眾聞子儀到，束甲來奔，歸者數萬。

translations.literal: The remaining troops, hearing Ziyi had arrived, girded armor and came to submit; those who returned numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When the remaining troops heard that Guo Ziyi had arrived, they donned their armor and came over—tens of thousands returned.

sentences.zh: 懷恩至靈武，嘯聚亡命，其眾復振。

translations.literal: Huai'en reached Lingwu, rallied outlaws by whistle-gathering; his forces revived again.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu, Huai'en gathered fugitives and outlaws, and his forces recovered their strength.

sentences.zh: 上念其勛舊，不欲罪功臣，厚撫其家，懷恩終不從。

translations.literal: The emperor remembered his past merit, did not wish to punish a meritorious minister, lavishly comforted his family—Huai'en in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his old service, the emperor unwilling to punish a former hero, treated Huai'en's family with generous kindness—yet Huai'en still refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 其母月餘日竟以壽終。

translations.literal: His mother, after a little more than a month, in the end died a natural death of old age.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died of natural causes a little over a month later.

sentences.zh: 又遙授太師、兼中書令、大寧王，余並停。

translations.literal: Again, from afar he was appointed Grand Preceptor, concurrently Grand Councilor, Prince of Daning—all other appointments were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The court again invested him from afar as Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Councilor, and Prince of Daning; all other posts were revoked.

sentences.zh: 是秋為鄉導，誘吐蕃十萬入寇涇、邠州，祭來瑱之墓，自序云「俱遭放逐」。

translations.literal: That autumn he served as guide, luring one hundred thousand Tibetans to invade Jing and Bin prefectures, sacrificed at Lai Tian's tomb, and in his own preface wrote "both suffered banishment."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he guided a Tibetan army of one hundred thousand against Jing and Bin prefectures, performed rites at Lai Tian's tomb, and wrote in a preface, "We both suffered exile."

sentences.zh: 寇奉天、醴泉，郭子儀拒之而退。

translations.literal: They invaded Fengtian and Liquan; Guo Ziyi repulsed them and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders struck Fengtian and Liquan; Guo Ziyi drove them back.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，上征天下兵以防之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, the emperor mobilized troops from throughout the realm to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: In 765, the emperor called up troops from across the empire to defend against the invasion.

sentences.zh: 懷恩又糾合諸蕃，眾號二十萬，南犯京師：遣吐蕃之眾自北道先寇醴泉、奉天，任敷、鄭庭、郝德自東道寇奉先、同州，羌、渾、奴剌之眾自西道寇盩厔、鳳翔。

translations.literal: Huai'en again gathered the various barbarians, proclaimed a force of two hundred thousand, and marched south against the capital: he sent the Tibetan host by the northern route first to invade Liquan and Fengtian; Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, and Hao De by the eastern route to invade Fengxian and Tong Prefecture; the Qiang, Hun, and Nula peoples by the western route to invade Zhouzhi and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en rallied the frontier tribes again, claiming a force of two hundred thousand, and marched south on the capital. He sent the Tibetans along the northern route against Liquan and Fengtian; Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, and Hao De along the eastern route against Fengxian and Tongzhou; and Qiang, Hun, and Nula forces along the western route against Zhouzhi and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大駭，詔遣郭子儀屯涇陽，渾日進、白元光屯奉天，李光時進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝廷玉屯中渭橋，董秦屯東渭橋，駱奉先、李日越屯盩厔，李抱玉屯鳳翔，周智光、杜冕屯同州。

translations.literal: The court was greatly alarmed; an edict dispatched Guo Ziyi to encamp at Jingyang, Hun Rijin and Bai Yuanguang at Fengtian, Li Guang Shijin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Central Wei Bridge, Dong Qin at Eastern Wei Bridge, Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue at Zhouzhi, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang, Zhou Zhiguang and Du Mian at Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court was terrified and ordered Guo Ziyi to hold Jingyang; Hun Rijin and Bai Yuanguang at Fengtian; Li Guang Shijin at Yunyang; Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Central Wei Bridge; Dong Qin at Eastern Wei Bridge; Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue at Zhouzhi; Li Baoyu at Fengxiang; and Zhou Zhiguang and Du Mian at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 上親率六軍，令魚朝恩屯苑中，下詔親征。

translations.literal: The emperor personally led the Six Armies, ordered Yu Chao'en to encamp in the imperial park, and issued an edict for a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally took command of the Six Armies, stationed Yu Chao'en in the imperial park, and proclaimed that he would lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 懷恩領回紇及朔方之眾繼進，行至鳴沙縣，遇疾舁歸。

translations.literal: Huai'en led the Uyghur and Shuofang troops in continued advance; reaching Mingsha County, he fell ill and was carried back.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en led the Uyghurs and Shuofang troops forward, but fell ill at Mingsha County and was carried back.

sentences.zh: 九月九日，死於靈武，部曲以鄉法焚而葬之。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month, he died at Lingwu; his retainers by native custom burned and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth Festival he died at Lingwu, and his troops cremated and buried him according to their tribal custom.

sentences.zh: 張韶代領其眾，為徐璜玉所殺；

translations.literal: Zhang Shao succeeded in leading his host and was killed by Xu Huangyu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao took command of his forces but was killed by Xu Huangyu;

sentences.zh: 璜玉領其眾，又為范志誠所殺，志誠領其眾。

translations.literal: Huangyu led his host, again was killed by Fan Zhicheng; Zhicheng led his host.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyu assumed command, only to be killed by Fan Zhicheng, who then took over the troops.

sentences.zh: 回紇進寇涇陽，諸軍堅壁不戰。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs advanced to invade Jingyang; the various armies fortified their walls and did not engage.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs pressed Jingyang, but the imperial armies held their positions and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃相持二十餘日，又聞懷恩死，與回紇爭長，自相疑貳，莫敢先進，遂大掠居人，焚燒舍宇，驅男女數萬而去，所過踐禾穀殆盡。

translations.literal: The Tibetans stood off for over twenty days; again they heard Huai'en was dead, vied with the Uyghurs for leadership, mutually grew suspicious and divided, none dared advance first; thereupon they greatly plundered residents, burned dwellings, drove off tens of thousands of men and women and departed, and wherever they passed they trampled grain nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days in stalemate, the Tibetans heard of Huai'en's death. They quarreled with the Uyghurs over command, grew mutually suspicious, and none dared advance first. They looted the countryside, burned homes, and drove off tens of thousands of civilians before retreating, trampling the harvest along the way.

sentences.zh: 回紇乃詣子儀降，請擊吐蕃以自效。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs then went to Ziyi to surrender, requesting to attack the Tibetans to prove their merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs then came to Guo Ziyi to surrender and offered to attack the Tibetans to prove their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子儀分兵隨之，大破吐蕃於涇州界。

translations.literal: Ziyi divided his troops to follow them and greatly defeated the Tibetans at the Jing Prefecture border.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent detachments with them and routed the Tibetans on the borders of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 任敷又敗走，羌、渾又多降於李抱玉。

translations.literal: Ren Fu again was defeated and fled; many of the Qiang and Hun surrendered to Li Baoyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu fled in defeat, and many Qiang and Hun tribes surrendered to Li Baoyu.

sentences.zh: 懷恩逆命三年，再犯順，連諸蕃之眾，為國大患，士不解甲，糧盡饋軍，適幸天亡，而上為之隱惡，前後下制，未嘗言其反。

translations.literal: Huai'en for three years defied orders, twice violated allegiance, linked the various barbarians' hosts, and became a great calamity for the state; soldiers did not ungird armor, grain was exhausted supplying the army—by good fortune Heaven destroyed him, yet the emperor concealed his evil; in edicts issued before and after, never once spoke of his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en had defied the throne for three years, rebelled twice, and united the frontier peoples into a national crisis. Soldiers never laid down their arms, and the granaries were drained to supply the armies. Heaven's mercy spared the dynasty when he died, yet the emperor still covered his crimes—even in successive edicts, he never acknowledged that Huai'en had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及懷恩死，群臣以聞，上為之憫默曰：「懷恩不反，為左右所誤。」

translations.literal: When Huai'en died, the ministers reported it; the emperor for this fell silent in compassion and said: "Huai'en did not rebel—he was misled by those at his side."
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers reported Huai'en's death, the emperor fell silent in sorrow and said, "Huai'en did not rebel. He was led astray by those around him."

sentences.zh: 其寬仁如此。

translations.literal: His leniency and benevolence were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his clemency.

sentences.zh: 閏十月，懷恩侄名臣領千餘騎來降。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month, Huai'en's nephew Mingchen led over a thousand horsemen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month, Huai'en's nephew Mingchen arrived with more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi

sentences.zh: 梁崇義，長安人。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi was a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi was a native of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以升斗給役於市，有膂力，能卷金舒鉤。

translations.literal: For a measure of grain per day he performed labor in the marketplace; he had physical strength and could bend gold and uncoil hooks.
translations.idiomatic: He hired himself out in the marketplace for a daily ration of grain. He was powerfully built and could bend metal bars and straighten iron hooks.

sentences.zh: 後為羽林射生，從來瑱於襄陽。

translations.literal: Later he became an Imperial Guard archer and followed Lai Tian to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became an archer in the Imperial Guard and served under Lai Tian at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 沈默寡言，眾悅之，累遷為偏裨。

translations.literal: Silent and sparing of words, the troops delighted in him; he was repeatedly promoted to subordinate commander.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and reserved, he won the men's affection and rose steadily to become a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 瑱朝京師，分使諸將戍福昌、南陽。

translations.literal: Tian went to court at the capital, dividing his generals to garrison Fuchang and Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Tian went to the capital, he sent his generals to garrison Fuchang and Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 來瑱被誅，戍者皆潰歸。

translations.literal: Lai Tian was executed; the garrison troops all dispersed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Lai Tian was executed, the garrison troops broke ranks and returned home.

sentences.zh: 崇義時在南陽，統歸師徑入襄州，與同列李昭、薛南陽相讓為長，不決。

translations.literal: Chongyi was then at Nanyang; gathering the returning troops he went straight into Xiang Prefecture, and with his peers Li Zhao and Xue Nanyang mutually yielded the position of chief—no resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was at Nanyang at the time. He gathered the returning troops and marched straight into Xiangzhou. He and his fellow officers Li Zhao and Xue Nanyang each deferred leadership to the others without reaching a decision.

sentences.zh: 諸將請曰：「兵非梁卿主之不可。」

translations.literal: The generals requested, saying: "The troops cannot be without Master Liang as chief."
translations.idiomatic: The officers pleaded, "Only you can command these troops, Lord Liang."

sentences.zh: 遂推崇義為帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon they elevated Chongyi as commander.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon made Chongyi their commander.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年三月，崇義殺昭與南陽，以脅眾心，朝廷因授其節度焉。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Baoying, Chongyi killed Zhao and Nanyang to intimidate the troops' hearts; the court thereupon invested him with the military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In March 763, Chongyi killed Zhao and Xue Nanyang to intimidate his followers, and the court duly appointed him military governor.

sentences.zh: 以襄州薦履兵禍，屈法含容，姑務息人也。

translations.literal: Because Xiang Prefecture had repeatedly suffered the calamity of warfare, the law was bent in forbearance—for the moment the task was to bring peace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiangzhou had suffered repeated warfare, the court bent the law in indulgence, seeking above all to restore peace.

sentences.zh: 歷御史中丞、大夫、尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as Censor Commissioner-in-Chief, Grand Counselor, and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Censor-in-Chief, Grand Counselor, and Minister.

sentences.zh: 遂與田承嗣、李正己、薛嵩、李寶臣為輔車之勢，奄有襄、漢七州之地，帶甲二萬，連結根固，未嘗朝覲，然於群凶，地最褊，兵最少，法令最理，禮貌最恭。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, Xue Song, and Li Baochen he formed a mutually dependent posture, suddenly holding the lands of seven prefectures of Xiang and Han, with twenty thousand armored troops, linked and rooted firm, never having attended court audience—yet among the band of villains his territory was narrowest, troops fewest, laws most ordered, and courtesy most deferential.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, Xue Song, and Li Baochen in mutual dependence, holding seven prefectures across the Xiang and Han region with twenty thousand soldiers. Though rooted in a firm network of alliances and never once attending court, among the rebel warlords his domain was the smallest, his army the weakest, yet his administration the most orderly and his deference the most scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 其地跨東南之沖，數有王命之所宣洽，故其人知化。

translations.literal: His territory straddled the strategic pass of the southeast; repeatedly imperial commands were promulgated there—thus its people knew civilization.
translations.idiomatic: His territory lay at a strategic crossroads of the southeast, where imperial authority had long been felt, and its people were well accustomed to civilization.

sentences.zh: 所親嘗勸其來朝，崇義曰：「吾本帥來公有大勛庸，當上元中以閹豎讒讟，逡巡稽召，及代宗嗣位，不俟駕行，旋見誅族。

translations.literal: Those close to him once urged him to come to court. Chongyi said: "My original commander Lord Lai had great merit; in the Shangyuan era due to eunuchs' slander, he lingered and delayed his response to summons; when Emperor Daizong succeeded the throne, without awaiting the imperial carriage he set out—and soon saw his clan executed.
translations.idiomatic: His intimates once urged him to attend court. Chongyi replied, "My old commander Lai Tian rendered great service to the dynasty. During the Shangyuan period, eunuchs slandered him until he hesitated to obey a recall. When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Lai set out without waiting for the imperial procession—and was swiftly executed along with his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 今吾釁盈而事久，若之何見上。」

translations.literal: Now my offense is full and my tenure long—how could I appear before the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Now my offenses are many and my rule has lasted too long. How could I possibly face the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 建中元年，淮西節度使李希烈數請興師討崇義，崇義懼，軍旅之事加嚴焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Huai West Military Governor Li Xilie repeatedly requested to raise troops to campaign against Chongyi; Chongyi was fearful, and military affairs were tightened further.
translations.idiomatic: In 780, Li Xilie, military governor of Huai West, repeatedly petitioned to launch a campaign against Chongyi. Chongyi grew alarmed and tightened military discipline.

sentences.zh: 流人郭昔告其為變，崇義聞之，請罪昔，坐決杖配流，命金部員外郎李舟諭旨以安之。

translations.literal: The exiled man Guo Xi reported that he would rebel; hearing this, Chongyi requested to punish Xi—Xi was sentenced to beating with the rod and exile; the court ordered Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Li Zhou to convey an imperial message to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: An exile named Guo Xi accused him of plotting rebellion. When Chongyi heard this, he demanded that Xi be punished. Xi was flogged and banished, and the court sent Li Zhou, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, to reassure Chongyi with an imperial message.

sentences.zh: 初，劉文喜作難，舟嘗入其城說利害，文喜拘之，會帳下殺文喜而降。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Wenxi rebelled, Zhou had once entered his city to explain advantage and harm; Wenxi detained him, but then his subordinates killed Wenxi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Wenxi rebelled, Li Zhou had entered his city to argue the stakes. Wenxi detained him, but his officers soon killed Wenxi and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 四方反側者聞之，謂舟必能覆軍殺將，是以皆惡。

translations.literal: Rebels throughout the four directions, hearing this, said Zhou could surely overturn armies and kill generals, and therefore all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious commanders everywhere, hearing of this, believed Zhou could topple armies and kill generals, and so they all distrusted him.

sentences.zh: 及舟至，又勸其入覲，言頗切直，崇義益不悅。

translations.literal: When Zhou arrived, he again urged Chongyi to enter court; his words were quite blunt and direct, and Chongyi grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou arrived, he again urged Chongyi to come to court in blunt, direct terms, which displeased Chongyi all the more.

sentences.zh: 二年春，發五使宣諭諸道，而舟復如荊、襄，崇義慮有變，拒境不納，上言「軍中疑懼，請換他使」。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year, five envoys were dispatched to proclaim edicts to the various circuits, and Zhou again went to Jing and Xiang. Chongyi feared there would be a change, refused entry at the border, and memorialized that "the army is suspicious and afraid—please exchange for another envoy."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 781, five envoys were sent to announce imperial orders to the circuits. When Zhou again went to Jing and Xiang, Chongyi, fearing trouble, barred the border and asked that another envoy be sent because "the troops are uneasy."

sentences.zh: 由是益不安，凶謀日深，賓僚或有忠言沮勸，多遭傷害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he grew still more uneasy; treacherous designs deepened daily, and advisers who offered loyal counsel were often harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He grew increasingly anxious, his plots deepened by the day, and advisers who spoke honestly were often punished.

sentences.zh: 時群凶方自疑阻，朝廷將仗大信，欲來而安之，以示天下。

translations.literal: At that time the various villains were themselves mutually suspicious and obstructed; the court wished to rely on great trust, intending to have them come and be reassured, to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel warlords were mutually suspicious, and the court wished to win them with great trust, hoping to summon them to court for reassurance as a signal to the empire.

sentences.zh: 仍加崇義同平章事，其妻子悉加封賞，且賜鐵券誓之，兼授其裨將藺杲為鄧州刺史，遣御史張著賚手詔征之。

translations.literal: Chongyi was further made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs; his wife and children were all given added enfeoffments and rewards, and an iron certificate was bestowed as oath. His deputy Lin Gao was also appointed governor of Deng Prefecture, and Censor Zhang Zhu was sent bearing a personal edict to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs. His wife and children received honors and rewards, and he was given an iron certificate of immunity. His deputy Lin Gao was appointed governor of Dengzhou, and Censor Zhang Zhu was sent with a personal edict summoning him to court.

sentences.zh: 崇義益恐怖，使持滿而受命。

translations.literal: Chongyi grew still more terrified and accepted the commission with bow drawn full.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was terrified and accepted the commission as though with an arrow on the string.

sentences.zh: 藺杲奉詔書，又不敢發，馳詣崇義請命，崇義益疑懼，對著號哭，不受詔。

translations.literal: Lin Gao received the edict document but again did not dare set out; he galloped to Chongyi to request orders. Chongyi grew still more suspicious and afraid; facing Zhu he wailed and refused the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Gao received the edict but dared not leave, and rode to Chongyi for instructions. Chongyi grew more fearful still, wept before Zhang Zhu, and refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 由是征四方兵，使希烈統擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon troops from the four directions were mobilized and Xilie was ordered to command the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court then mobilized armies from all directions and ordered Li Xilie to command the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 崇義乃發兵攻江陵，以通黔、嶺，及四望，大敗而歸，遂屯襄、鄧。

translations.literal: Chongyi thereupon sent troops to attack Jiangling to open a route to Qian and Ling, and to Siwang; he was thoroughly defeated and returned, then encamped at Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi then attacked Jiangling to open routes toward Qian, Ling, and Siwang, was routed, and withdrew to hold Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 希烈先發千餘人守臨漢，崇義屠之，無遺噍。

translations.literal: Xilie first sent more than a thousand men to hold Linhan; Chongyi slaughtered them, leaving none to chew.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie had first sent more than a thousand men to hold Linhan; Chongyi massacred them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 既而希烈統大軍緣漢而上，崇義使將翟暉、杜少誠迎戰於蠻水，希烈大破之；

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Xilie led a great army up the Han River. Chongyi sent generals Zhai Hui and Du Shaocheng to meet the fight at Manshui; Xilie thoroughly defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xilie led a large force up the Han. Chongyi sent Zhai Hui and Du Shaocheng to fight at Manshui, and Xilie routed them;

sentences.zh: 復合於涑口，又破之。

translations.literal: They joined battle again at Shukou and were again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Shukou and were beaten once more.

sentences.zh: 二將求降，希烈受之，使統本兵入襄陽號令，以安百姓。

translations.literal: The two generals sought to surrender; Xilie accepted them and had them command their original troops to enter Xiangyang and proclaim orders, to settle the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The two generals offered to surrender. Xilie accepted them and sent them with their troops into Xiangyang to restore order for the populace.

sentences.zh: 崇義領親兵老小閉壁，將守者斬關爭出，不可止。

translations.literal: Chongyi led his personal troops, old and young, to shut the walls; the defenders cut the gate bars and struggled to get out—it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi shut himself in with his family and personal troops, but the garrison broke the gates and rushed out in a panic that could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，崇義與其妻投井而死，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Chongyi and his wife threw themselves into a well and died; their heads were transmitted to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year Chongyi and his wife threw themselves into a well. Their heads were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其親戚希烈皆戮之，選其嘗從臨漢之役者三千人，悉斬之。

translations.literal: His relatives were all executed by Xilie; three thousand who had once followed the campaign at Linhan were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie executed his relatives and beheaded three thousand men who had served at Linhan.

sentences.zh: 李懷光

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang

sentences.zh: 李懷光，渤海靺鞨人也。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang was a Mohe man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang was a Mohe tribesman from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 本姓茹，其先徙於幽州，父常為朔方列將，以戰功賜姓氏，更名嘉慶。

translations.literal: His original surname was Ru; his ancestors had migrated to You Prefecture. His father Chang served as a lieutenant of Shuofang and, for military achievement, was granted the imperial surname and renamed Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: His clan name was originally Ru. His forebears had moved to Youzhou. His father Chang was a Shuofang officer and, for military merit, was granted the imperial surname and renamed Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 懷光少從軍，以武藝壯勇稱，朔方節度使郭子儀禮之益厚。

translations.literal: Huaiguang joined the army young and was famed for martial skill and brave strength; Shuofang military governor Guo Ziyi treated him with ever greater courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang entered the army young and was known for martial prowess and courage. Guo Ziyi, governor of Shuofang, treated him with exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 上元中，累遷試太僕、太常卿，主右衙兵將，積功勞至開府儀同三司，為朔方軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and acting chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, commanding the right-wing army generals; through accumulated merit he reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with independent office and became deputy commander of the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan period he rose to acting Grand Master of the Imperial Stud and acting chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, commanding generals of the right wing. Through accumulated merit he became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with an independent office and deputy commander of the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he received an actual fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongtai era he received a substantive fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大曆六年，兼御史中丞，間一年，兼御史大夫，加為軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dali he was made concurrent Censor Commissioner-in-Chief; after one year, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and additionally army deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 771 he was made concurrent Censor Commissioner-in-Chief. A year later he became Censor-in-Chief and army deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 性清勤嚴猛，而敢誅殺，雖親戚犯法，皆不撓避。

translations.literal: His nature was clear, diligent, stern, and fierce, and he dared to execute and kill; even when relatives violated the law he did not yield or avoid.
translations.idiomatic: He was scrupulous, stern, and fierce, and did not shrink from executing even relatives who broke the law.

sentences.zh: 子儀性寬厚，不親軍事，紀綱任懷光，軍中尤畏之，亦稱為理。

translations.literal: Ziyi's nature was generous and he did not personally attend to military affairs; discipline was entrusted to Huaiguang, and within the army he was especially feared—he was also called able in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was easygoing and left military discipline to Huaiguang. The troops feared him above all others, yet they also called his rule just.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以母憂罷職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 777 he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年，起復本官，仍兼邠、寧、慶三州都將。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled to his original post and still held the post of commander-in-chief of Bin, Ning, and Qing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to his former post and also commanded the armies of Bin, Ning, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，罷子儀節度副元帥，以其所部分隸諸將，遂以懷光起復檢校刑部尚書，兼河中尹、邠州刺史、邠寧慶晉降慈隰節度支度營田觀察押諸蕃部落等使。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, Ziyi's post as deputy commander-in-chief was abolished and his forces were divided among the various generals. Huaiguang was then recalled from mourning as acting Minister of Justice, concurrent governor of Hedong, governor of Bin Prefecture, and military governor of Bin-Ning-Qing-Jin-Jiang-Ci-Luo with responsibility for garrison, farming, observation, and the frontier tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, Guo Ziyi's deputy command was abolished and his troops divided among other generals. Huaiguang was recalled from mourning as acting Minister of Justice, concurrent governor of Hedong and Binzhou, and military governor over Bin, Ning, Qing, and neighboring circuits with authority over garrisons, farming, frontier tribes, and transport.

sentences.zh: 先是，懷光頻歲率師城長武以處軍士，城據原首，臨涇水，俯瞰通道，吐蕃自是不敢南侵，為西邊要防矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huaiguang for successive years had led troops to build the fortress at Changwu to house soldiers. The fortress stood on the plateau head overlooking the Jing River and commanded the routes below; the Tibetans from this did not dare invade south, and it became a key defense of the western border.
translations.idiomatic: For years Huaiguang had led troops to build a fortress at Changwu to quarter his soldiers. It stood on the high ground above the Jing River, commanding the passes below, so that Tibetans dared not raid southward. It became a vital western defense.

sentences.zh: 建中初，涇原四鎮節度使段秀實為宰相楊炎所惡，徵為司農卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Jingyuan Fourth Circuit military governor Duan Xiushi was hated by chief minister Yang Yan and was summoned as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era, Duan Xiushi, governor of the Jingyuan Fourth Circuit, was hated by Chief Minister Yang Yan and was recalled as Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 上將復城原州，乃以懷光兼涇州刺史、涇原四鎮北庭節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to rebuild Yuan Prefecture fortress and thereupon made Huaiguang concurrent governor of Jing Prefecture and military governor of Jingyuan Fourth Circuit and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to rebuild the fortress at Yuanzhou and made Huaiguang concurrent governor of Jingzhou and military governor of the Jingyuan Fourth Circuit and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 時懷光挾私怨，親誅殺朔方舊將溫儒雅等數人，涇州軍士咸畏之。

translations.literal: At that time Huaiguang bore private resentment and personally executed several old Shuofang generals including Wen Ruya; the Jingzhou soldiers all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huaiguang, nursing private grievances, personally executed several veteran Shuofang officers including Wen Ruya, and the Jingzhou troops all feared him.

sentences.zh: 劉文喜因眾不欲，遂以城叛。

translations.literal: Liu Wenxi, because the masses did not wish it, thereupon rebelled with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops would not accept him, Liu Wenxi rebelled and held the city.

sentences.zh: 詔朱泚與懷光將兵討平之，加檢校太子少師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhu Ci and Huaiguang to lead troops to pacify him; he was additionally made acting Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhu Ci and Huaiguang to suppress the rebellion and made Huaiguang acting Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷檢校左僕射，兼靈州大都督、單于鎮北大都護、朔方節度支度營田觀察鹽池押諸蕃部落六城水運使，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent chief administrator of Lingzhou, Chanyu Protector-General of the North, Shuofang military governor with responsibility for farming, salt ponds, frontier tribes, and the six-city water transport commissioner, with an actual fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 781 he was promoted to acting Left Vice Director, concurrent chief administrator of Lingzhou, Chanyu Protector-General of the North, and Shuofang governor with authority over farming, salt ponds, frontier tribes, and water transport, with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度等使如故。

translations.literal: His posts as Bin-Ning military governor and the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: His Bin-Ning governorship and other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧、李抱真諸軍同討魏城未拔，硃滔、王武俊皆反，連兵救悅。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui, Li Baoyu, and other armies together were campaigning against Weicheng without taking it; Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun had both rebelled and joined forces to relieve Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Sui and Li Baoyu were besieging Weicheng without success, while Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun had rebelled and marched to relieve Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔遣懷光統朔方兵步騎一萬五千同討田悅。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered Huaiguang to command fifteen thousand Shuofang infantry and cavalry jointly to attack Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In 782 an edict ordered Huaiguang to lead fifteen thousand Shuofang foot and horse soldiers against Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 懷光勇而無謀，至魏城之日，營壘未設，因與滔等大戰於愜山，為滔等所敗。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was brave but without strategy; on the day he reached Weicheng the encampments were not yet set, and he fought a great battle with Tao and the others at Qieshan and was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was brave but lacked strategy. The day he reached Weicheng his camp was not yet pitched, and he fought Zhu Tao and the others at Qieshan and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 復為悅決水以灌之，諸軍不利，因與燧等退軍於魏縣。

translations.literal: Yue again breached the dikes to flood them; the various armies were disadvantaged and therefore withdrew with Sui and the others to Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue then broke the dikes to flood them. The imperial armies fared badly and withdrew with Ma Sui to Weixian.

sentences.zh: 尋加同平章事，益實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with an added actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with an added fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 自是與滔等相持不戰。

translations.literal: From this he and Tao and the others faced off without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he and Zhu Tao's forces faced each other without engaging.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，涇原之卒叛，上居奉天。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the next year the Jingyuan troops rebelled and the emperor resided at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year the Jingyuan troops mutinied and the emperor took refuge at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 朱泚既僭大號，遣中使馳告河北諸帥，懷光率軍奔命。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had already usurped the imperial title and sent palace envoys posthaste to notify the Hebei military governors; Huaiguang led his army in desperate haste to answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had declared himself emperor and sent envoys to the Hebei governors. Huaiguang marched his army to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 時屬泥淖，懷光奮厲軍士，道自蒲津渡河，敗泚騎兵於醴泉，直赴奉天。

translations.literal: It happened to be muddy and mired; Huaiguang roused his soldiers strenuously, taking the route from Pujin to cross the river, defeated Ci's cavalry at Liquan, and went straight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were deep in mud, but Huaiguang drove his men hard, crossed at Pujin, routed Zhu Ci's cavalry at Liquan, and pressed on to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 前數日，先遣裨將張韶持表封蠟丸隨賊攻城，乘間逾塹，呼城上人曰：「朔方軍使也。」

translations.literal: Several days earlier he had first sent deputy general Zhang Shao bearing a sealed memorial in a wax pill to follow the rebels in attacking the city; seizing an interval he leaped the moat and called to those on the wall: "Shuofang army envoy!"
translations.idiomatic: Days earlier he had sent his deputy Zhang Shao with a sealed memorial in a wax pellet to infiltrate the rebel siege. Seizing a moment, Shao leaped the moat and shouted to the defenders, "Envoy from the Shuofang army!"

sentences.zh: 乃以繩引上城而入，比登堞，身中數十矢。

translations.literal: He was then drawn up by rope onto the wall and entered; by the time he climbed the parapet his body had taken dozens of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him up by rope onto the wall. By the time he reached the parapet he had been struck by dozens of arrows.

sentences.zh: 時上在重圍中，守拒益急，既知懷光軍至，令張韶號令於城上，人心乃安。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was in heavy encirclement and defense grew ever more urgent; once he knew Huaiguang's army had arrived, he had Zhang Shao proclaim orders on the wall and the people's hearts were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in desperate straits and the siege grew tighter. When he learned that Huaiguang's army had arrived, he had Zhang Shao announce it from the wall, and the defenders' hearts were steadied.

sentences.zh: 懷光又敗泚兵於魯店，泚乃解兵還走入城。

translations.literal: Huaiguang again defeated Ci's troops at Ludian; Ci thereupon disbanded his army and withdrew into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang defeated Zhu Ci's troops again at Ludian, and Ci broke off the siege and withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 懷光性粗厲疏愎，緣道數言盧杞、趙贊、白志貞等奸佞，且曰：「天下之亂，皆此輩也，吾見上，當請誅之。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang's nature was coarse, fierce, negligent, and obstinate. Along the road he repeatedly spoke of the treachery of Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, Bai Zhizhen, and others, saying: "The turmoil of the realm is all due to these men. When I see the emperor I shall request their execution."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was rough, fierce, and stubborn. Marching along the road he denounced Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, Bai Zhizhen, and others as traitors, saying, "These men brought the empire to ruin. When I see the emperor I will ask that they be executed."

sentences.zh: 杞等微知之，懼甚，因說上令懷光乘勝逐泚，收復京師，不可許至奉天，德宗從之。

translations.literal: Qi and the others learned of this in slight measure and were greatly afraid; they therefore persuaded the emperor to have Huaiguang pursue Ci with the momentum of victory and recover the capital, and not permit him to come to Fengtian. Dezong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and his allies learned of it and were terrified. They persuaded the emperor to send Huaiguang to pursue Zhu Ci and retake the capital, but not to let him come to Fengtian. Dezong agreed.

sentences.zh: 懷光屯軍咸陽，數上表暴揚杞等罪惡，上不得已為貶杞、趙贊、白志貞以慰安之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang encamped his army at Xianyang and repeatedly submitted memorials exposing the crimes of Qi and the others; the emperor had no choice but to demote Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang camped at Xianyang and repeatedly memorialized the throne exposing Qi and the others. The emperor was forced to demote Qi, Zhao Zan, and Bai Zhizhen to placate him.

sentences.zh: 又疏中使翟文秀，上之信任也，又殺之。

translations.literal: He also denounced the palace envoy Zhai Wenxiu, whom the emperor trusted, and again executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced the palace envoy Zhai Wenxiu, whom the emperor trusted, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 懷光既不敢進軍，遷延自疑，因謀為亂。

translations.literal: Huaiguang, daring not advance his army, delayed and grew self-suspicious, and thereupon plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to advance and growing suspicious, Huaiguang plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 初，詔遣崔漢衡使於吐蕃，出兵佐收京城，蕃相尚結贊曰：「蕃法，進軍以統兵大臣為信。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had dispatched Cui Hengheng as envoy to the Tibetans to send troops to assist in recovering the capital. The Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan said: "By Tibetan law, advance requires the name of the commander who leads the army as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had sent Cui Hengheng to the Tibetans to ask for troops to retake the capital. The Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan said, "By Tibetan law we need the name of the commanding general on the imperial order before we can march.

sentences.zh: 今奉制書，無懷光名署，故不敢前。」

translations.literal: Now the edict received bears no signature of Huaiguang's name, and therefore we dare not advance."
translations.idiomatic: This edict bears no signature of Huaiguang, so we dare not advance."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣翰林學士陸贄詣懷光議用蕃軍，懷光堅執言不可者三，不肯署制，詞慢，且謂贄曰：「爾何所能？」

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and sent Hanlin academician Lu Zhi to Huaiguang to discuss using Tibetan troops. Huaiguang firmly held that it could not be done three times, refused to sign the edict, spoke with contempt, and said to Zhi: "What ability do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hanlin academician Lu Zhi to discuss Tibetan aid with Huaiguang. Three times Huaiguang refused, would not sign the edict, spoke insolently, and said to Lu Zhi, "What can you do?"

sentences.zh: 興元元年二月，詔加太尉，兼賜鐵券，遣李升及中使鄧鳴鶴賚券喻旨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xingyuan an edict added Grand Preceptor and bestowed an iron certificate; Li Sheng and the palace envoy Deng Minghe were sent bearing the certificate to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 784 an edict made him Grand Preceptor and granted an iron certificate. Li Sheng and the envoy Deng Minghe were sent to present it.

sentences.zh: 懷光怒甚，投券於地曰：「凡人臣反，則賜鐵券，今授懷光，是使反也。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang was exceedingly angry, threw the certificate to the ground, and said: "When a minister rebels, then an iron certificate is bestowed. Now giving it to Huaiguang is to make him rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was furious, threw the certificate to the ground, and said, "Iron certificates are given to rebels. Giving me one means you want me to rebel."

sentences.zh: 詞氣益悖，眾為之懼。

translations.literal: His tone grew still more perverse and all were afraid for it.
translations.idiomatic: His words grew still more defiant, and everyone was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時懷光部將韓遊瑰掌兵在奉天，懷光乃與遊瑰書，約令為變，遊瑰密奏之。

translations.literal: At that time Huaiguang's subordinate general Han Yougui held troops at Fengtian. Huaiguang wrote to Yougui arranging for him to mutiny; Yougui secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's subordinate Han Yougui commanded troops at Fengtian. Huaiguang wrote urging him to rebel, but Yougui reported the plot secretly.

sentences.zh: 翌日，懷光又使趣之，遊瑰復奏聞。

translations.literal: The next day Huaiguang again sent to urge him; Yougui again reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huaiguang urged him again, and Yougui reported once more.

sentences.zh: 數日，懷光又使趣遊瑰，為門者所捕。

translations.literal: Several days later Huaiguang again sent to urge Yougui; the messenger was captured at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Huaiguang sent another urgent message, and the messenger was seized at the gate.

sentences.zh: 懷光且宣言曰：「吾今與朱泚連和，車駕當須引避。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang thereupon proclaimed: "I now join with Zhu Ci in alliance; the imperial carriage must withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang then announced, "I am allied with Zhu Ci. The emperor must leave."

sentences.zh: 由是上遽幸梁州。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor hastily went to Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurriedly fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時李晟已移軍東渭橋，懷光復劫李建徽、楊惠元等軍，移於好畤，其下頗多攜貳。

translations.literal: At that time Li Sheng had already moved his army to Eastern Wei Bridge. Huaiguang again seized the armies of Li Jianhui, Yang Huiyuan, and others, moved to Haochi, and among his subordinates many wavered in divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng had already moved to Eastern Wei Bridge. Huaiguang seized the forces of Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan and withdrew to Haochi, while many of his officers wavered.

sentences.zh: 先是朱泚甚畏之，至是因欲臣之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu Ci had greatly feared him; now because of this he wished to make him a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had once feared him greatly; now he sought to win him as an ally.

sentences.zh: 懷光虜劫無所得，益疑懼不自安，居二旬，乃驅兵分為部隊，掠涇陽、三原、富平，自同州往河中。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's plundering gained nothing; he grew still more suspicious and afraid and ill at ease. After twenty days he drove his troops in divided columns, raiding Jingyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping, and went from Tong Prefecture toward Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His raids yielded little. Growing more fearful and uneasy, after twenty days he split his army to plunder Jingyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping, then marched from Tongzhou toward Hedong.

sentences.zh: 神策將孟涉、段威勇自三原擁兵三千餘人奔歸李晟，懷光不能遏。

translations.literal: Shence generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong from Sanyuan led more than three thousand troops in flight to join Li Sheng; Huaiguang could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Shence generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong led more than three thousand men from Sanyuan to Li Sheng, and Huaiguang could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰殺懷光留後張昕，以邠州從順。

translations.literal: Han Yougui killed Huaiguang's rear-guard commander Zhang Xin and submitted Bin Prefecture in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui killed Huaiguang's rear commander Zhang Xin and submitted Binzhou to the court.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏自奉天令於軍曰：「懷光已反。」

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan from Fengtian ordered the army, saying: "Huaiguang has rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan at Fengtian announced to the troops, "Huaiguang has rebelled."

sentences.zh: 乃令城守馳表以聞。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the city defended and sent a rapid memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified the city and sent an urgent report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上於是授遊瑰、休顏節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon invested Yougui and Xiuyan as military governors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Yougui and Xiuyan as military governors.

sentences.zh: 乃除懷光太子太保，罷其餘官，其所管委本軍擇一人功高望崇者統之，皆不奉詔。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was then made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and his other offices were abolished. His command was entrusted to this army to choose one man of lofty achievement and high standing to command—all did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was reduced to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and stripped of his other posts. The court ordered his army to choose a respected commander, but none obeyed.

sentences.zh: 四月，懷光至河中，遂偷有同、絳等州，按兵觀望。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Huaiguang reached Hedong and thereupon seized Tong, Jiang, and other prefectures by stealth, holding his troops in observation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he reached Hedong and quietly seized Tong, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures, holding his army in reserve.

sentences.zh: 李晟既收復京師，上遣給事中孔巢父、中使啖守盈持詔征之，懷光素服受命。

translations.literal: After Li Sheng had recovered the capital, the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Kong Chaofu and the palace envoy Tan Shouying bearing an edict to summon him; Huaiguang at first received it in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Sheng recovered the capital, the emperor sent Kong Chaofu and Tan Shouying with an edict summoning him. Huaiguang at first received it submissively.

sentences.zh: 巢父乃宣言於眾：「太尉軍中誰可領軍事者？」

translations.literal: Chaofu thereupon proclaimed to the masses: "In the Grand Preceptor's army, who can take command of military affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu then asked the assembly, "Who in the Grand Preceptor's army can take command?"

sentences.zh: 懷光左右皆胡虜，因發怒，亂持兵殺巢父及守盈，自是繕兵益修守拒。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's attendants were all barbarians; they thereupon flew into rage, wildly seized weapons and killed Chaofu and Shouying. From this he repaired arms ever more and strengthened defense and resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's guards were mostly non-Chinese. Enraged, they seized weapons and killed Chaofu and Shouying. From then on Huaiguang strengthened his defenses.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，以侍中渾瑊為河中節度副元帥，將兵討懷光。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he appointed Palace Attendant Hun Zhen as deputy commander-in-chief of Hedong and sent troops to campaign against Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Chang'an he named Palace Attendant Hun Zhen deputy commander of Hedong and sent him against Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 瑊復破同州，屯軍不進，數為懷光所敗。

translations.literal: Zhen again took Tong Prefecture and encamped his army without advancing, repeatedly being defeated by Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Zhen retook Tongzhou but halted his advance and was beaten repeatedly by Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 時仍歲旱蝗，京師初復，經費不給，言事者多請赦懷光。

translations.literal: At that time drought and locusts struck year after year; the capital had just been restored and funds were insufficient; many who spoke on affairs requested amnesty for Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and locusts persisted, the capital had only just been restored, and funds were scarce. Many officials urged the emperor to pardon Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 時河東、節度使馬燧威名素著，乃加燧副元帥，與瑊及鎮國軍節度駱元光、邠寧節度韓遊瑰、鄜坊節度唐朝臣會兵同討懷光。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong military governor Ma Sui's martial renown was always lofty; he was thereupon made deputy commander-in-chief together with Zhen, Zhenguo military governor Luo Yuanguang, Bin-Ning military governor Han Yougui, and Yan-Fang military governor Tang Chaochen to unite armies and jointly campaign against Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui of Hedong was famed for his military prowess and was made deputy commander with Hun Zhen, Luo Yuanguang of Zhenguo, Han Yougui of Bin-Ning, and Tang Chaochen of Yan-Fang to campaign against Huaiguang jointly.

sentences.zh: 燧率軍拔絳州，至寶鼎，慮懷光西走，唐突京邑，乃舍軍朝京師。

translations.literal: Sui led his army to take Jiang Prefecture and reached Baoding. Fearing Huaiguang would flee west and suddenly strike the capital, he left his army and went posthaste to court.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui took Jiangzhou and reached Baoding, but fearing Huaiguang might strike west toward the capital, he left his army and hurried to court.

sentences.zh: 既還，與瑊先自河東而降其驍將尉珪、徐庭光，統諸軍以圍河中。

translations.literal: After returning, together with Zhen he first from Hedong induced his fierce generals Wei Gui and Xu Tingguang to surrender, and united the armies to besiege Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he and Hun Zhen first induced Huaiguang's fierce generals Wei Gui and Xu Tingguang to surrender from Hedong, then united the armies to besiege Hedong.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年秋，朔方部將牛名俊斬懷光首以降燧瑊隹刃其弟數人，乃自殺。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Zhenyuan, Shuofang subordinate Niu Mingjun beheaded Huaiguang and surrendered. Sui and Zhen then stabbed several of his younger brothers and he thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 785, Shuofang officer Niu Mingjun beheaded Huaiguang and surrendered. Ma Sui and Hun Zhen executed several of his brothers, after which he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 懷光死時年五十七。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang died he was fifty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was fifty-seven when he died.

sentences.zh: 尋詔以男一人為嗣，賜莊宅各一所，仍還懷光屍首，任其收葬，妻子並徙澧州。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter an edict made one son his heir, bestowed one manor and one residence each, returned Huaiguang's corpse for burial as they wished, and exiled wife and children to Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon named one son as heir, granted a manor and residence, returned Huaiguang's body for burial, and exiled his wife and children to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，又詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year another edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year another edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 懷舊念功，仁之大也；

translations.literal: Cherishing the old and remembering merit is the greatest benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: To cherish old service and remember merit is the height of benevolence;

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，義之弘也。

translations.literal: to revive what is extinguished and continue what is broken is the broadest righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: to revive the fallen and continue broken lines is the broadest righteousness.

sentences.zh: 昔蔡叔圮族，周公封其子於東土；

translations.literal: In antiquity the Duke of Cai's clan was destroyed, yet the Duke of Zhou enfeoffed his son in the eastern lands;
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Cai's house was destroyed, the Duke of Zhou enfeoffed his son in the east;

sentences.zh: 韓信幹紀，漢後爵其孥以弓高。

translations.literal: Han Xin violated discipline, yet the Han later ennobled his descendants at Gonggao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin rebelled, yet the Han later ennobled his kin at Gonggao.

sentences.zh: 侯君集之不率景化，我太宗存其胤以主祀。

translations.literal: Hou Junji did not follow the transforming influence of the age, yet our Taizong preserved his descendants to maintain the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji turned against the throne, yet Emperor Taizong preserved his line to maintain the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 詳考先王之道，洎乎烈祖之訓，皆以刑佐德，俾人向方，則斧鉞之誅，甲兵之伐，蓋不得已而用也。

translations.literal: Examining in detail the way of former kings down to the instructions of the glorious ancestors, all used punishment to assist virtue and cause men to turn toward the correct direction. Thus the executioner's axe and the dispatch of armed forces were employed only when there was no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the ways of the ancient kings and our glorious ancestors, punishment assists virtue and turns men toward righteousness. The axe and the army are used only when there is no other way.

sentences.zh: 曩歲盜臣竊發，國步多虞，朕狩於近郊，指期薄伐，將振昆陽之旅，以興涿鹿之功，征師未達於諸侯，衛士且疲於七萃。

translations.literal: In years past rebellious ministers rose in theft and the state's steps had many troubles. I hunted in the near suburbs and fixed a date for the punitive campaign, intending to rouse the host of Kunyang and achieve the merit of Zhuolu. The campaign army had not yet reached the feudal lords and the guards were already weary in the seven musters.
translations.idiomatic: In years past rebels rose and the throne was imperiled. I took the field near the capital, intending to repeat the rescue of Kunyang and the victory at Zhuolu. Yet before the armies arrived my guards were already exhausted.

sentences.zh: 而李懷光三軍夙駕，千里勤王，上假雷霆之威，下逐虎狼之眾。

translations.literal: Yet Li Huaiguang's three armies had long hastened forth and for a thousand li labored in the king's cause, above borrowing the thunder's might, below driving the host of tiger and wolf.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Huaiguang's armies had marched a thousand li to save the throne, lending Heaven's thunder above and driving the rebel host below.

sentences.zh: 議功方始，守節靡終，潛構禍胎，拒違朝命，棄同即異，舍順效逆。

translations.literal: When merit was just being weighed he did not preserve his integrity to the end, secretly framing the womb of calamity, refusing and violating court commands, abandoning unity for division, leaving obedience for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were being weighed he failed to remain loyal, secretly bred treason, defied the court, abandoned unity for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 為臣至此，在法必誅，猶示綏懷，庶其牽復。

translations.literal: As a minister reaching this point, by law he must be executed; yet we still showed soothing reassurance, hoping he might be drawn back.
translations.idiomatic: For such conduct the law demands death, yet we still showed mercy, hoping he would return.

sentences.zh: 而梟音益厲，狶突莫遷，大戮所加，曾無噍類。

translations.literal: Yet his owl cry grew ever fiercer and his boar charge would not shift; what the great punishment added left not even a class to chew.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he grew only more defiant, and when the full penalty fell none of his house survived.

sentences.zh: 雖自貽伊戚，與眾棄之，而言念爾勞，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Though he brought calamity on himself and was abandoned by the masses, speaking of your labors—alas, too late!
translations.idiomatic: Though he brought ruin on himself and was cast off by all, when I think of your service—alas, too late!

sentences.zh: 以其前效猶在，孤魂無歸，懷之怳然，是用悽軫。

translations.literal: Because your former achievement still stands and your lone soul has no return, cherishing this I am dazed; therefore I am deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Because your early merit still stands and your spirit has no home, I am moved to deep grief.

sentences.zh: 予欲布陳大惠，冀以化成，保合太和，期於刑措。

translations.literal: I wish to spread great favor, hoping thereby to transform, preserving great harmony and expecting the time when punishment may be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to spread great grace, hoping to transform by it, preserve universal harmony, and reach the age when punishments are unused.

sentences.zh: 宜以懷光外孫燕八八賜姓李氏，名承緒，授左衛率府胄曹參軍，承懷光之後。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's maternal grandson Yan Babai should be granted the surname Li, named Chengxu, appointed Army Guard Office Retainer, and made to continue Huaiguang's line.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's grandson Yan Babai shall take the surname Li, be named Chengxu, appointed retainer in the Army Guard Office, and continue Huaiguang's line.

sentences.zh: 仍賜錢一千貫，任於懷光墓側置立莊園，侍養懷光妻王氏，並備四時享奠之禮。

translations.literal: One thousand strings of cash are further bestowed to establish a manor beside Huaiguang's tomb to support his wife Lady Wang and provide the rites of offering in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: A grant of one thousand strings of cash shall establish a manor by Huaiguang's tomb to support his wife Lady Wang and provide seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 朕實不德，臨於兆人，泣辜宥罪，素誠所志。

translations.literal: My virtue is truly insufficient; facing the myriad people, weeping over the guilty and pardoning crimes—this is the plain sincerity of my aim.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is insufficient before the people. To mourn the guilty and pardon crimes is the aim of my heart.

sentences.zh: 爾其保姓受氏，宣力承家，勉紹乃考之建國庸，無若爾父之違王命。

translations.literal: You must preserve your surname and receive your clan, proclaim strength and sustain your house, strive to continue your father's founding merit to the state, and be not like your father in violating the king's command.
translations.idiomatic: Preserve your clan, serve the house, strive to continue your father's merit to the state, and do not follow your father in defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，懷光授首，其子琟、瑗等皆死，唯妻王氏在，故上特舍其死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huaiguang's head was taken, his sons Wei, Yuan, and the rest all died; only his wife Lady Wang survived, and therefore the emperor specially spared her life.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang was killed his sons Wei and Yuan and the rest had all died; only his wife Lady Wang survived, and the emperor spared her.

sentences.zh: 及是又思懷光舊勛，哀其絕後，乃命承緒繼之。

translations.literal: At this he again thought of Huaiguang's old merit, pitied that his line was cut off, and thereupon ordered Chengxu to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now, remembering Huaiguang's old service and pitying his extinguished line, the emperor ordered Chengxu to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：仆固懷恩、李懷光，咸以勇力，有勞王家，為臣不終，遂行反噬，其罪大矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Pugu Huai'en and Li Huaiguang both relied on courage and strength and labored for the royal house. As ministers they did not finish; they thereupon turned to rebellion and devouring—their crime was great.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Pugu Huai'en and Li Huaiguang both served the dynasty with martial valor. Neither finished loyal; both turned to rebellion. Their crimes were grave.

sentences.zh: 然辛雲京、駱奉先、盧杞、白志貞輩，致彼二逆，貽憂時君，亦可謂國之讒賊矣。

translations.literal: Yet Xin Yunjing, Luo Fengxian, Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, and their kind brought those two rebels into being and left worry for the rulers of the age—they too may be called slanderous villains of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xin Yunjing, Luo Fengxian, Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, and their like provoked these two rebellions and troubled the throne—they too were villains of the state.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義既無令始，又無善終，與妻投泉，何塞其咎。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi had neither a good beginning nor a good end; with his wife he cast themselves into a spring—how could that cover his guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi had neither a good beginning nor a good end. He and his wife threw themselves into a well—how could that expiate his guilt?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：臣之事君，有死無二。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In serving the ruler a minister has death but no duality.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: A minister serves his ruler with loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 懷恩、懷光，凶終一致。

translations.literal: Huai'en and Huaiguang—violent endings in one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en and Huaiguang met the same violent end.

sentences.zh: 崇義多奸，國家所棄。

translations.literal: Chongyi was full of treachery; the state cast him off.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was treacherous, and the state cast him off.

sentences.zh: 迷而亡歸，自速其斃。

translations.literal: Lost and with no return, he hastened his own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Lost, with nowhere to turn, he rushed to his own ruin.
